sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第128卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 128
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 128

sentences.zh: 【宋紀十】 起閼逢敦牂，盡著雍閹茂，凡五年。

translations.literal: [Song Records 10] — From Quefeng Dunziang through Zhuyong Yanmao, five years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Song Records 10] — From the year jiawu (454) through the year wuxu (458), five years in all.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝武皇帝上孝建元年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu the Founding Ancestor, upper fascicle — first year of Xiaojian (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu, upper fascicle — the first year of Xiaojian (

sentences.zh: 甲午，公元四五四年）

translations.literal: jiawu, the year 454 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jiawu, 454 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己亥朔，上祀南郊，改元，大赦。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the first day of the month (jihai), the Emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar, changed the era name, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the new moon of the first month (day jihai), the emperor performed the southern suburban sacrifice, declared the new era name, and issued a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以尚書令何尚之為左光祿大夫、護軍將軍，以左衛將軍顏竣為吏部尚書、領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: On jiachen, He Shangzhi was made Left Master of Splendid Happiness and Protector of the Army from Minister of the Masters of Writing; Yan Jun was made Minister of the Civil Office and concurrent Commander of the Rapid Cavalry from Left Defender General.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, He Shangzhi moved from Minister of the Masters of Writing to Left Master of Splendid Happiness and Protector of the Army, while Yan Jun rose from Left Defender General to Minister of the Civil Office with concurrent command of the Rapid Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，更鑄孝建四銖錢。

translations.literal: On renxu, the Xiaojian four-zhu coins were recast.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, the government recast the new Xiaojian four-zhu coin.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，魏以侍中伊□為司空。

translations.literal: On yichou, Wei made Palace Attendant Yi □ Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Northern Wei appointed Palace Attendant Yi [name damaged in the source] Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 丙子，立皇子子業為太子。

translations.literal: On bingzi, the imperial son Ziye was established as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, the emperor named his son Ziye crown prince.

sentences.zh: 初，江州刺史臧質，自謂人才足為一世英雄；

translations.literal: Initially, Zang Zhi, Governor of Jiang Province, considered his talent sufficient to be a hero of an age;
translations.idiomatic: Early on, Zang Zhi, governor of Jiangzhou, held himself fit to stand as a hero of the age;

sentences.zh: 太子劭之亂，質潛有異圖，以荊州刺史南郡王義宣庸暗易制，欲外相推奉，因而覆之。

translations.literal: During the rebellion of Crown Prince Shao, Zhi secretly harbored a different design; he regarded the Prince of Nanjun, Liu Yixuan, Governor of Jing Province, as dull and easy to control, and wished to promote him outwardly while overthrowing him in turn.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Shao rebelled, Zhi secretly nursed designs of his own. He judged Liu Yixuan, Prince of Nanjun and governor of Jingzhou, dull and easy to manage, and planned to raise him up publicly only to overturn him afterward.

sentences.zh: 質於義宣為內兄，既至江陵，即稱名拜義宣。

translations.literal: Zhi was Yixuan's brother-in-law; once he reached Jiangling, he at once bowed to Yixuan by personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was Yixuan's brother-in-law; as soon as he reached Jiangling he bowed to Yixuan by personal name alone.

sentences.zh: 義宣驚愕問故，質曰：「事中宜然。」

translations.literal: Yixuan, startled, asked the reason. Zhi said, "In the present affair it is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan asked in astonishment why; Zhi replied, "Given how matters stand, this is only proper."

sentences.zh: 時義宣已奉帝為主，故其計不行。

translations.literal: By then Yixuan had already acknowledged the Emperor as sovereign, so his plan could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: But Yixuan had already accepted the emperor as rightful ruler, so the scheme came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 及至新亭，又拜江夏王義恭，曰：「天下屯危，禮異常日。」

translations.literal: When he reached Xinting, he again bowed to Liu Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, saying, "The realm is in dire peril; ritual differs from ordinary days."
translations.idiomatic: At Xinting he bowed likewise to Liu Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, saying, "The empire stands in grave peril; ceremony cannot be what it was in ordinary times."

sentences.zh: 劭既誅，義宣與質功皆第一，由是驕恣，事多專行，凡所求欲，無不必從。

translations.literal: After Shao was executed, Yixuan and Zhi ranked first in merit; from this they grew arrogant and willful, acting on their own in many matters, and whatever they sought was invariably granted.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shao was dead, Yixuan and Zhi stood foremost in merit. They grew arrogant and high-handed, doing as they pleased in most affairs, and every request they made was granted.

sentences.zh: 義宣在荊州十年，財富兵強；

translations.literal: Yixuan had been in Jing Province ten years, rich in wealth and strong in troops;
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan had governed Jingzhou for ten years and was rich in wealth and strong in arms;

sentences.zh: 朝廷所下制度，意有不同，一不遵承。

translations.literal: whenever the court issued regulations with which he disagreed in mind, he followed none of them.
translations.idiomatic: whenever court regulations did not suit him, he refused to obey them altogether.

sentences.zh: 質自建康之江州，舫千餘乘，部伍前後百餘里。

translations.literal: Zhi traveled from Jiankang to Jiang Province with more than a thousand boats; his retinue stretched over a hundred li before and behind.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi went from Jiankang to Jiangzhou he took more than a thousand boats, and his column stretched for over a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 帝方自攬威權，而質以少主遇之，政刑慶賞，一不咨稟。

translations.literal: The Emperor was just then gathering power into his own hands, yet Zhi treated him as a young sovereign; in punishments, rewards, and policy he consulted and reported on nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was only beginning to gather power into his own hands, yet Zhi treated him as a mere boy on the throne and never sought approval for rewards, punishments, or policy.

sentences.zh: 擅用湓口、鉤圻米，台符屢加檢詰，漸致猜懼。

translations.literal: He appropriated grain from Pankou and Gouqi on his own authority; the central offices repeatedly sent orders of investigation, and suspicion and fear gradually arose.
translations.idiomatic: He seized grain from Pankou and Gouqi without authorization; the central government repeatedly investigated, and mutual suspicion grew.

sentences.zh: 帝淫義宣諸女，義宣由是恨怒。

translations.literal: The Emperor debauched several of Yixuan's daughters; Yixuan therefore hated and raged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took Yixuan's daughters for his pleasure, and Yixuan came to hate him with burning anger.

sentences.zh: 質乃遣密信說義宣，以為：「負不賞之功，挾震主之威，自古能全者有幾？

translations.literal: Zhi then sent a secret letter to persuade Yixuan, saying, "Bearing merit beyond reward and wielding awe that shakes the ruler — since antiquity how many have preserved themselves whole?
translations.idiomatic: Zhi sent a secret message urging Yixuan on: "You hold merit too great to be rewarded and power that terrifies the throne. How many men in history have survived that?

sentences.zh: 今萬物系心於公，聲跡已著；

translations.literal: Now all things hang their hearts on you; your fame and track are already manifest;
translations.idiomatic: All hearts already turn to you, and your renown is plain for all to see;

sentences.zh: 見幾不作，將為它人所先。

translations.literal: if you see the moment and do not act, others will get ahead of you.
translations.idiomatic: if you see your opening and fail to move, someone else will seize it first.

sentences.zh: 若命徐遺寶、魯爽驅西北精兵來屯江上，質帥九江樓船為公前驅，已為得天下之半。

translations.literal: If you order Xu Yibao and Lu Shuang to drive the elite troops of the northwest to camp on the Yangzi, and Zhi leads the tower-ships of Jiujiang as your vanguard, you will already have half the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Order Xu Yibao and Lu Shuang to bring the northwest's best troops down to the Yangzi, and let me lead Jiujiang's war fleet as your vanguard — you will already hold half the empire.

sentences.zh: 公以八州之眾，徐進而臨之，雖韓、白更生，不能為建康計矣。

translations.literal: With the masses of eight provinces you advance slowly and press upon them; even if Han Xin and Bai Qi were reborn, they could not devise a plan for Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Then advance at leisure with the armies of eight provinces. Even if Han Xin and Bai Qi rose again, they could not save Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 且少主失德，聞於道路；

translations.literal: Moreover the young sovereign lacks virtue, known on the roads;
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the young emperor's misconduct is common talk on every road;

sentences.zh: 沈、柳諸將，亦我之故人，誰肯為少主盡力者？

translations.literal: the generals Shen and Liu are also my old associates — who will exert himself to the utmost for the young sovereign?
translations.idiomatic: Generals Shen and Liu are old friends of mine as well. Who will fight his heart out for this boy on the throne?

sentences.zh: 夫不可留者年也，不可失者時也。

translations.literal: What cannot be detained is the year; what cannot be missed is the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Years cannot be held back, and opportunity cannot be missed.

sentences.zh: 質常恐溘先朝露，不得展其旅力，為公掃除，於時悔之何及。」

translations.literal: Zhi often fears he will die before the morning dew and be unable to deploy his host's strength to sweep clear the way for you — by then regret will come too late."
translations.idiomatic: I fear I may die before the dew dries and never bring my troops to clear your path — and then regret will be useless."

sentences.zh: 義宣腹心將佐咨議參軍蔡超、司馬竺超民等咸有富貴之望，欲倚質威名以成其業，共勸義宣從其計。

translations.literal: Yixuan's trusted aides — Consulting Adviser Cai Chao and Chief of Staff Zhu Chaomin — all hoped for wealth and rank and wished to lean on Zhi's prestige to accomplish their aims; together they urged Yixuan to follow the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan's closest advisers, Cai Chao and Zhu Chaomin, all hungered for wealth and power and hoped to ride Zhi's reputation to their goals; together they pressed Yixuan to agree.

sentences.zh: 質女為義宣子采之婦。

translations.literal: Zhi's daughter was wife to Yixuan's son Caizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's daughter was married to Yixuan's son Caizhi.

sentences.zh: 義宣謂質無復異同，遂許之。

translations.literal: Yixuan judged that Zhi would not again differ, and so consented.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan believed Zhi would not waver again and gave his assent.

sentences.zh: 超民，夔之子也。

translations.literal: Chaomin was the son of Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Chaomin was a son of Kui.

sentences.zh: 臧敦時為黃門侍郎，帝使敦至義宣所，道經尋陽，質更令敦說誘義宣，義宣意遂定。

translations.literal: Zang Dun was then Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates; the Emperor sent Dun to Yixuan's place. Passing through Xunyang, Zhi further had Dun persuade and entice Yixuan, and Yixuan's mind was settled."
translations.idiomatic: Zang Dun, then a Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, was sent by the emperor to visit Yixuan. Passing Xunyang, Zhi had him press the case again, and Yixuan's resolve hardened.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史魯爽有勇力，義宣、質素與之相結。

translations.literal: Lu Shuang, Governor of Yu Province, had courage and strength; Yixuan and Zhi had long been allied with him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang, governor of Yuzhou, was bold and powerful; Yixuan and Zhi had long been tied to him.

sentences.zh: 義宣密使人報爽及兗州刺史徐遺寶，期以今秋同舉兵。

translations.literal: Yixuan secretly sent men to inform Shuang and Xu Yibao, Governor of Yan Province, fixing this autumn for a joint rising.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan secretly notified Shuang and Xu Yibao, governor of Yanzhou, to rise together that autumn.

sentences.zh: 使者至壽陽，爽方飲醉，失義宣指，即日舉兵。

translations.literal: When the messenger reached Shouyang, Shuang was drunk and missed Yixuan's intent; that very day he raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy reached Shouyang while Shuang was drunk. Missing Yixuan's meaning, he rose in arms that same day.

sentences.zh: 爽弟瑜在建康，聞之，逃叛。

translations.literal: Shuang's younger brother Yu was in Jiankang; hearing this, he fled in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang's brother Yu was in Jiankang; on hearing the news he fled.

sentences.zh: 爽使其眾戴黃標，竊造法服，登壇，自號建平元年；

translations.literal: Shuang had his troops wear yellow badges, secretly made regalia, ascended the altar, and styled himself first year of Jianping;
translations.idiomatic: Shuang had his men wear yellow markers, secretly made imperial regalia, mounted the altar, and declared the first year of Jianping;

sentences.zh: 疑長史韋處穆、中兵參軍楊元駒、治中庾騰之不與己同，皆殺之。

translations.literal: suspecting Chief Clerk Wei Chumu, Central Army Major Yang Yuanju, and Administrator Yu Tengzhi of not sharing his purpose, he killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: suspecting Chief Clerk Wei Chumu, Army Major Yang Yuanju, and Administrator Yu Tengzhi of disloyalty, he had them all killed.

sentences.zh: 遺寶亦勒兵向彭城。

translations.literal: Yibao also mustered troops toward Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yibao likewise marched his troops toward Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 二月，義宣聞爽已反，狼狽舉兵。

translations.literal: Second month: Yixuan heard Shuang had already rebelled and raised troops in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, hearing that Shuang had already risen, Yixuan hurriedly took up arms.

sentences.zh: 魯瑜弟弘為質府佐，帝敕質收之，質即執台使，舉兵。

translations.literal: Lu Yu's younger brother Hong was an aide in Zhi's headquarters; the Emperor ordered Zhi to seize him, and Zhi at once arrested the court envoy and raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu's brother Hong served on Zhi's staff. When the emperor ordered Zhi to arrest him, Zhi seized the imperial envoy instead and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 義宣與質皆上表，言為左右所讒疾，欲誅君側之惡。

translations.literal: Yixuan and Zhi both submitted memorials saying they had been slandered by those at the ruler's side and wished to execute the evil beside the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan and Zhi both memorialized the throne, claiming they had been slandered by the emperor's intimates and wished only to purge evil from the court.

sentences.zh: 義宣進爽號征北將軍。

translations.literal: Yixuan advanced Shuang's title to General Who Conquers the North.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan promoted Shuang to General Who Conquers the North.

sentences.zh: 爽於是送所造輿服詣江陵，使征北府戶曹版義宣等，文曰：「丞相劉，今補天子，名義宣；

translations.literal: Shuang then sent the regalia he had made to Jiangling and had the Household Bureau of the Northern Expedition headquarters issue commissions for Yixuan and others, the text reading, "Chancellor Liu is now appointed Son of Heaven, personal name Yixuan;
translations.idiomatic: Shuang sent the regalia he had made to Jiangling and had his Northern Expedition staff issue commissions reading, "Chancellor Liu is now appointed Son of Heaven, personal name Yixuan;

sentences.zh: 東騎臧，今補丞相，名質；

translations.literal: Eastern Cavalryman Zang is now appointed Chancellor, personal name Zhi;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Cavalryman Zang is now appointed Chancellor, personal name Zhi;

sentences.zh: 平西朱，今補車騎，名修之。

translations.literal: Pacifier of the West Zhu is now appointed Chariots and Cavalry General, personal name Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifier of the West Zhu is now appointed Chariots and Cavalry General, personal name Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 皆版到奉行。」

translations.literal: All commissions are to be obeyed upon arrival."
translations.idiomatic: All commissions take effect upon delivery."

sentences.zh: 義宣駭愕，爽所送法物並留竟陵，不聽進。

translations.literal: Yixuan was appalled; he detained all the regalia Shuang sent at Jingling and would not allow them forward.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan was horrified. He kept all the regalia Shuang sent at Jingling and refused to let them proceed.

sentences.zh: 質加魯弘輔國將軍，下戍大雷。

translations.literal: Zhi promoted Lu Hong to General Who Supports the State and posted him to garrison Dalei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi made Lu Hong General Who Supports the State and stationed him at Dalei.

sentences.zh: 義宣遣咨議參軍劉諶之將萬人就弘，召司州刺史魯秀，欲使為諶之後繼。

translations.literal: Yixuan sent Consulting Adviser Liu Chenzhi with ten thousand men to join Hong and summoned Lu Xiu, Governor of Si Province, intending him as Chenzhi's rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan sent Liu Chenzhi with ten thousand men to reinforce Hong and summoned Lu Xiu, governor of Sizhou, to follow up behind Chenzhi.

sentences.zh: 秀至江陵見義宣，出，拊膺曰：「吾兄誤我，乃與癡人作賊，今年敗矣！」

translations.literal: Xiu reached Jiangling, saw Yixuan, and on leaving beat his breast, saying, "My elder brother has misled me — to make a rebel with a fool! This year we are ruined!"
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu reached Jiangling and met Yixuan, he left beating his breast. "My brother has ruined me," he cried. "Rebelling with a fool — we are finished this year!"

sentences.zh: 義宣兼荊、江、兗、豫四州之力，威震遠近。

translations.literal: Yixuan combined the strength of the four provinces Jing, Jiang, Yan, and Yu; his prestige shook far and near.
translations.idiomatic: With the combined power of Jing, Jiang, Yan, and Yuzhou behind him, Yixuan's might awed the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝欲奉乘輿法物迎之，竟陵王誕固執不可，曰：「奈何持此座與人！」

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to send the imperial carriage and regalia to welcome him; the Prince of Jingling, Dan, firmly refused, saying, "How can we hand this throne to another!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to send the imperial carriage and regalia to welcome him, but Prince Dan of Jingling objected firmly: "How can we hand this throne away!"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: And so it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: And so the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以領軍將軍柳元景為撫軍將軍；

translations.literal: On jimao, Liu Yuanjing, General of the Palace Guards, was made General Who Pacifies the Army;
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Liu Yuanjing, commander of the palace guards, was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army;

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以左衛將軍王玄謨為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: on xinmao, Wang Xuanmo, Left Defender General, was made Governor of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: on xinmao, Wang Xuanmo, Left Defender General, was made governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 命元景統玄謨等諸將以討義宣。

translations.literal: Yuanjing was ordered to command Xuanmo and the other generals to attack Yixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing was ordered to lead Xuanmo and the other generals against Yixuan.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，進據梁山洲，於兩岸築偃月壘，水陸待之。

translations.literal: On guisi, he advanced and held Liangshan Isle, building crescent fortifications on both banks to await them by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi he advanced to Liangshan Isle and built crescent fortifications on both banks to block them by land and water.

sentences.zh: 義宣自稱都督中外諸軍事，命僚佐悉稱名。

translations.literal: Yixuan styled himself Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Inside and Outside and ordered his staff all to address him by personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan styled himself supreme commander of all armies and required his staff to address him by personal name alone.

sentences.zh: 甲午，魏主詣道壇受圖菉。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the Wei ruler went to the Dao altar to receive the talismanic registers.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, the Wei emperor went to the Daoist altar to receive the sacred registers.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以安北司馬夏侯祖歡為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Xiahou Zuhuan, Chief of Staff of the Army Pacifying the North, was made Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Xiahou Zuhuan was appointed governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，己亥，內外戒嚴。

translations.literal: Third month, on jihai, martial law was proclaimed inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jihai, the court proclaimed martial law throughout the capital and provinces.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以徐州刺史蕭思話為江州刺史，柳元景為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Xiao Sihua, Governor of Xu Province, was made Governor of Jiang Province; Liu Yuanjing was made Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Xiao Sihua moved from Xuzhou to Jiangzhou, and Liu Yuanjing was appointed governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以太子左衛率龐秀之為徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On guimao, Pang Xiuzhi, Leader of the Crown Prince's Left Guard, was made Governor of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Pang Xiuzhi was appointed governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 義宣移檄州郡，加進位號，使同發兵。

translations.literal: Yixuan circulated proclamations to the provinces and commanderies, advancing titles and ranks and ordering them to rise together.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan sent proclamations through the provinces, promoting ranks and calling on all to take up arms.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史朱修之偽許之，而遣使陳誠於帝。

translations.literal: Zhu Xiuzhi, Governor of Yong Province, feigned assent but sent envoys to declare his loyalty to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi, governor of Yongzhou, pretended to agree but sent envoys pledging loyalty to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史劉秀之斬義宣使者，遣中兵參軍韋崧將萬人襲江陵。

translations.literal: Liu Xiuzhi, Governor of Yi Province, executed Yixuan's envoy and sent Central Army Major Wei Song with ten thousand men to strike Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiuzhi of Yizhou killed Yixuan's envoy and sent Wei Song with ten thousand men to raid Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 戊申，義宣帥眾十萬發江津，舳艫數百里。

translations.literal: On wushen, Yixuan led a host of one hundred thousand from Jiangjin; the line of boats stretched hundreds of li.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Yixuan led a hundred thousand men from Jiangjin; his fleet stretched for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 以子慆為輔國將軍，與左司馬竺超民留鎮江陵。

translations.literal: His son Tao was made General Who Supports the State; he and Left Chief of Staff Zhu Chaomin were left to guard Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He left his son Tao as General Who Supports the State, with Zhu Chaomin, to hold Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 檄朱修之使發兵萬人繼進，修之不從。

translations.literal: He summoned Zhu Xiuzhi to send ten thousand men in follow-up; Xiuzhi did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zhu Xiuzhi to follow with ten thousand men; Xiuzhi refused.

sentences.zh: 義宣知修之貳於己，乃以魯秀為雍州刺史，使將萬餘人擊之。

translations.literal: Knowing Xiuzhi was disloyal to him, Yixuan made Lu Xiu Governor of Yong Province and sent him with more than ten thousand men to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Xiuzhi had turned against him, Yixuan appointed Lu Xiu governor of Yongzhou and sent him with over ten thousand men to attack him.

sentences.zh: 王玄謨聞秀不來，喜曰：「臧質易與耳！」

translations.literal: Wang Xuanmo heard Xiu would not come and rejoiced, saying, "Zang Zhi will be easy to deal with!"
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xuanmo heard that Xiu would not come, he exclaimed with delight, "Zang Zhi will be easy meat!"

sentences.zh: 冀州刺史垣護之妻，徐遺寶之姊也，遺寶邀護之同反，護之不從，發兵擊之。

translations.literal: The wife of Yuan Huzhi, Governor of Ji Province, was Yibao's elder sister; Yibao invited Huzhi to rebel with him, but Huzhi refused and sent troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Huzhi, governor of Jizhou, was married to Yibao's sister. Yibao asked him to join the rebellion; Huzhi refused and attacked him.

sentences.zh: 遺寶遣兵襲徐州長史明胤於彭城，不克。

translations.literal: Yibao sent troops to strike Ming Yin, Chief Clerk of Xu Province, at Pengcheng, but did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Yibao sent troops against Ming Yin at Pengcheng but failed to take the city.

sentences.zh: 胤與夏侯祖歡、垣護之共擊遺寶於湖陸，遺寶棄眾焚城，奔魯爽。

translations.literal: Yin, together with Xiahou Zuhuan and Yuan Huzhi, jointly attacked Yibao at Hulu; Yibao abandoned his host, burned the city, and fled to Lu Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin joined Xiahou Zuhuan and Yuan Huzhi to defeat Yibao at Hulu. Yibao abandoned his army, burned the town, and fled to Lu Shuang.

sentences.zh: 義宣至尋陽，以質為前鋒而進，爽亦引兵直趣歷陽，與質水陸俱下。

translations.literal: Yixuan reached Xunyang and advanced with Zhi as vanguard; Shuang also led troops straight toward Liyang, descending with Zhi by land and water together.
translations.idiomatic: At Xunyang, Yixuan advanced with Zhi in the vanguard while Shuang marched straight on Liyang; land and river forces moved down together.

sentences.zh: 殿中將軍沈靈賜將百舸，破質前軍於南陵，擒軍主徐慶安等。

translations.literal: Palace General Shen Lingci led a hundred boats, defeated Zhi's vanguard at Nanling, and captured the commander Xu Qing'an and others.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Lingci led a hundred boats, smashed Zhi's vanguard at Nanling, and captured Xu Qing'an and other commanders.

sentences.zh: 質至梁山，夾陳兩岸，與官軍相拒。

translations.literal: Zhi reached Liangshan, deployed on both banks, and faced off against the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi reached Liangshan, drew up on both banks of the river, and faced the imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊辰，以後將軍劉義綦為湘州刺史；

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on wuchen, Liu Yiqi, Rear General, was made Governor of Xiang Province;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on wuchen, Liu Yiqi was appointed governor of Xiangzhou;

sentences.zh: 甲申，以朱修之為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: on jiashen, Zhu Xiuzhi was made Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: on jiashen, Zhu Xiuzhi was appointed governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 上遣左軍將軍薛安都、龍驤將軍南陽宗越等戍歷陽，與魯爽前鋒楊胡興等戰，斬之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Xue Andu, General of the Left Army, and Zong Yue of Nanyang, Dragon Cavalry General, and others to garrison Liyang; they fought Shuang's vanguard Yang Huxing and others and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Xue Andu and Zong Yue to hold Liyang. They met Lu Shuang's vanguard Yang Huxing and killed him.

sentences.zh: 爽不能進，留軍大峴，使魯瑜屯小峴。

translations.literal: Shuang could not advance; he left troops at Great Xian and had Lu Yu camp at Little Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang could not advance further. He left his army at Great Xian and posted Lu Yu at Little Xian.

sentences.zh: 上復遣鎮軍將軍沈慶之濟江，督諸將討爽；

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent Shen Qingzhi, General Who Pacifies the Army, across the river to supervise the generals in attacking Shuang;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Shen Qingzhi across the Yangzi to command the generals against Shuang;

sentences.zh: 爽食少，引兵稍退，自留斷後。

translations.literal: Shuang had little food and drew his troops back somewhat, himself remaining to cover the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Short of supplies, Shuang began to withdraw, staying behind to cover the retreat.

sentences.zh: 慶之使薛安都帥輕騎追之，丙戌，及爽於小峴。

translations.literal: Qingzhi had Xue Andu lead light cavalry in pursuit; on bingxu they caught Shuang at Little Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi sent Xue Andu with light cavalry in pursuit. On bingxu they caught Shuang at Little Xian.

sentences.zh: 爽將戰，飲酒過醉，安都望見爽，即躍馬大呼，直往刺之，應手而倒，左右范雙斬其首。

translations.literal: Shuang was about to fight but had drunk himself too drunk; Andu saw Shuang, leaped his horse, shouted, and ran straight to stab him — he fell at the blow, and Fan Shuang at his side cut off his head.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang prepared to fight but was drunk beyond measure. Andu spotted him, spurred forward with a shout, and ran him through at the first thrust. Fan Shuang then struck off his head.

sentences.zh: 爽眾奔散，瑜亦為部下所殺。

translations.literal: Shuang's host scattered in flight; Yu was also killed by his own subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang's army broke and fled; Yu was killed by his own men.

sentences.zh: 遂進攻壽陽，克之。

translations.literal: They then advanced to attack Shouyang and took it.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on to Shouyang and captured it.

sentences.zh: 徐遺寶奔東海，東海人殺之。

translations.literal: Xu Yibao fled to Donghai; the people of Donghai killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yibao fled to Donghai, where the locals killed him.

sentences.zh: 李延壽論曰：「凶人之濟其身，非世亂莫由焉。

translations.literal: Li Yannian remarked: "A vicious man preserves himself only when the age is in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yannian wrote: "A wicked man can save himself only in times of chaos.

sentences.zh: 魯爽以亂世之情，而行之於平日，其取敗也宜哉！

translations.literal: Lu Shuang applied the conduct of a chaotic age in ordinary times — it was fitting he met defeat!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang acted as if the empire were already in chaos while peace still held. Small wonder he was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 南郡王義宣至鵲頭，慶之送爽首示之，並與書曰：僕荷任一方，而釁生所統。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Nanjun, Yixuan, reached Que'tou, Qingzhi sent him Shuang's head for display and wrote with it: "Your servant bears charge of a region, yet trouble arose within what I govern."
translations.idiomatic: When Yixuan reached Que'tou, Qingzhi sent him Shuang's head and a letter: "I hold command in one region, yet rebellion broke out under my rule."

sentences.zh: 近聊帥輕師，指往翦撲，軍鋒裁及，賊爽授首。

translations.literal: Recently I briefly led a light army, aiming to go cut down and crush; the army's spear-tip had just reached when the rebel Shuang surrendered his head.
translations.idiomatic: I recently took a small force straight to strike him down; our vanguard had scarcely arrived when the rebel Shuang lost his head.

sentences.zh: 公情契異常，或欲相見，及其可識，指送相呈。」

translations.literal: Your emotional bond is exceptional; perhaps you wished to see him; while he can still be recognized, I send him for your viewing."
translations.idiomatic: Our bond runs deep; if you wished to see him while his face was still recognizable, I have sent his head for you to view."

sentences.zh: 爽累世將家，驍猛善戰，號萬人敵。

translations.literal: Shuang came from generations of military families, fierce and bold and skilled in battle, styled a match for ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang came from a long line of generals, fierce in battle and reckoned the equal of ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 義宣與質聞其死，皆駭懼。

translations.literal: Yixuan and Zhi, hearing of his death, were both struck with terror.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixuan and Zang Zhi heard that he was dead, both were shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 柳元景軍於採石；

translations.literal: Liu Yuanjing encamped at Caishi;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanjing had his army at Caishi;

sentences.zh: 王玄謨以臧質眾盛，遣使來求益兵，上使元景進屯姑孰。

translations.literal: Wang Xuemo, because Zang Zhi's forces were numerous, sent an envoy to request reinforcements; the Emperor had Yuanjing advance to garrison Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zang Zhi's army was large, Wang Xuemo sent an envoy asking for more troops, and the emperor ordered Yuanjing to move up and encamp at Gushu.

sentences.zh: 太傅義恭與義宣書曰：「往時仲堪假兵，靈寶尋害其族；

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yigong wrote to Yixuan, saying: "In former times Zhongkan borrowed troops, and Lingbao soon destroyed his clan;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yigong wrote to Yixuan: "In the past Yin Zhongkan borrowed troops, and Wang Lingbao soon wiped out his whole clan;

sentences.zh: 孝伯推誠，牢之旋踵而敗。

translations.literal: Xiaobo showed good faith, and Laozhi failed in the turning of a heel.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiaobo gave him his trust, and Liu Laozhi was ruined almost overnight.

sentences.zh: 臧質少無美行，弟所具悉。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi from youth had no fine conduct — you, my brother, know this fully.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi has lacked virtue since youth — you, my brother, know that as well as anyone.

sentences.zh: 今藉西楚之強力，圖濟其私；

translations.literal: Now relying on Western Chu's great strength, he seeks to fulfill his private aims;
translations.idiomatic: Now he is using Western Chu's power to serve his own ends;

sentences.zh: 凶謀若果，恐非復池中物也。」

translations.literal: If his wicked scheme succeeds, I fear he will no longer be a creature in the pond."
translations.idiomatic: If his wicked plot succeeds, I fear he will no longer be content to stay in the pond."

sentences.zh: 義宣由此疑之。

translations.literal: From this Yixuan came to suspect him.
translations.idiomatic: From this Yixuan began to distrust him.

sentences.zh: 五月，甲辰，義宣至蕪湖，質進計曰：「今以萬人取南州，則梁山中絕；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jiachen, Yixuan reached Wuhu; Zhi offered a plan, saying: "Now with ten thousand men take the southern region, and Liangshan will be cut off in the middle;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiachen, Yixuan reached Wuhu. Zhi proposed: "Send ten thousand men to seize the south, and Liangshan will be cut in two;

sentences.zh: 萬人綴梁山，則玄謨必不敢動；

translations.literal: Ten thousand men hold Liangshan, and Xuemo will surely not dare move;
translations.idiomatic: Hold Liangshan with ten thousand men, and Xuemo will not dare stir;

sentences.zh: 下官中流鼓棹，直趣石頭，此上策也。」

translations.literal: Your humble servant beats oars midstream and goes straight for Shitou — this is the superior stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: I will row up the river and strike straight at Shitou — that is the best plan."

sentences.zh: 義宣將從之。

translations.literal: Yixuan was about to follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan was on the point of agreeing.

sentences.zh: 劉諶之密言於義宣曰：「質求前驅，此志難測。

translations.literal: Liu Chenzhi spoke secretly to Yixuan, saying: "Zhi asks to be vanguard — this intent is hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chenzhi whispered to Yixuan: "Zhi wants the vanguard — his intentions are hard to read.

sentences.zh: 不如盡銳攻梁山，事克然後長驅，此萬安之計也。」

translations.literal: Better to concentrate all elite forces to attack Liangshan; once the affair succeeds, then drive forward at length — this is the plan of ten thousand safeties."
translations.idiomatic: Better to throw everything at Liangshan first and, once that is won, advance in force — that is the safest course."

sentences.zh: 義宣乃止。

translations.literal: Yixuan thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan then changed his mind.

sentences.zh: 冗從僕射鬍子反等守梁山西壘，會西南風急，質遣其將尹周之攻西壘；

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Hu Zifan and others defended the western fort of Liangshan; a southwest wind blew fiercely, and Zhi sent his general Yin Zhouzhi to attack the western fort;
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Hu Zifan and others held the western fort at Liangshan. A fierce southwest wind sprang up, and Zhi sent his general Yin Zhouzhi to assault the western fort;

sentences.zh: 子反方渡東岸就玄謨計事，聞之，馳歸。

translations.literal: Zifan was just crossing to the eastern bank to consult Xuemo on plans; hearing this, he raced back.
translations.idiomatic: Zifan had just crossed to the eastern bank to confer with Xuemo when he heard the news and galloped back.

sentences.zh: 周之攻壘甚急，偏將劉季之帥水軍殊死戰，求救於玄謨，玄謨不遣；

translations.literal: Zhouzhi pressed the fort attack fiercely; vice-general Liu Jizhi led the naval force in a desperate fight and begged Xuemo for aid; Xuemo did not send it;
translations.idiomatic: Zhouzhi pressed the attack hard. Vice-general Liu Jizhi fought to the death with the fleet and pleaded for help, but Xuemo refused to send any;

sentences.zh: 大司馬參軍崔勳之固爭，乃遣勳之與積弩將軍垣詢之救之。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal staff officer Cui Xunzhi argued forcefully, and only then were Xunzhi and Crossbow General Yuan Xunzhi sent to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal staff officer Cui Xunzhi protested vigorously, and at last Xuemo sent Xunzhi and Crossbow General Yuan Xunzhi to their aid.

sentences.zh: 比至，城已陷，勳之、詢之皆戰死。

translations.literal: By the time they arrived, the fort had already fallen; Xunzhi and Xunzhi both died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they arrived, the fort had already fallen, and both Xunzhi and Xunzhi were killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 詢之，護之之弟也。

translations.literal: Xunzhi was younger brother to Huzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzhi was the younger brother of Yuan Huzhi.

sentences.zh: 子反等奔還東岸。

translations.literal: Zifan and the others fled back to the eastern bank.
translations.idiomatic: Zifan and his men fled back to the eastern bank.

sentences.zh: 質又遣其將龐法起將數千兵趨南浦，欲自後掩玄謨，游擊將軍垣護之引水軍與戰，破之。

translations.literal: Zhi again sent his general Pang Faqi with several thousand troops toward Nanpu, intending to take Xuemo from the rear; Mobile General Yuan Huzhi led the naval force to fight and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi also sent his general Pang Faqi with several thousand men toward Nanpu to take Xuemo from behind, but Mobile General Yuan Huzhi met him with the fleet and routed him.

sentences.zh: 朱修之斷馬鞍山道，據險自守。

translations.literal: Zhu Xiuzhi cut off the road at Ma'anshan and held the perilous ground in self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi blocked the road at Ma'anshan and held the defensible ground.

sentences.zh: 魯秀攻之不克，屢為修之所敗，乃還江陵，修之引兵躡之。

translations.literal: Lu Xiu attacked but could not overcome him, was repeatedly defeated by Xiuzhi, then returned to Jiangling; Xiuzhi led troops in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiu attacked but failed to break him, was beaten again and again, and retreated to Jiangling; Xiuzhi pursued with his army.

sentences.zh: 或勸修之急追，修之曰：「魯秀，驍將也；

translations.literal: Some urged Xiuzhi to press the pursuit urgently; Xiuzhi said: "Lu Xiu is a fierce general;
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Xiuzhi to press the pursuit, but he said: "Lu Xiu is a formidable commander;

sentences.zh: 獸窮則攫，不可迫也。」

translations.literal: When a beast is cornered it will claw — one must not press it."
translations.idiomatic: A cornered beast will strike back — he must not be driven too hard."

sentences.zh: 王玄謨使垣護之告急於柳元景曰：「西城不守，唯餘東城萬人。

translations.literal: Wang Xuemo had Yuan Huzhi report the emergency to Liu Yuanjing, saying: "The western fort cannot be held; only ten thousand men remain in the eastern fort.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuemo sent Yuan Huzhi to Liu Yuanjing with an urgent appeal: "The western fort is lost; only ten thousand men remain in the eastern fort.

sentences.zh: 賊軍數倍，強弱不敵。

translations.literal: The rebel army is several times our size; strength and weakness are not matched.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy outnumbers us several times over; we cannot match their strength.

sentences.zh: 欲退還姑孰，就節下協力當之，更議進取。」

translations.literal: We wish to withdraw to Gushu, join forces under Your Excellency to meet them, and discuss advance anew."
translations.idiomatic: We wish to fall back to Gushu, join your forces, and then decide how to advance again."

sentences.zh: 元景不許，曰：「賊勢方盛，不可先退，吾當卷甲赴之。」

translations.literal: Yuanjing did not permit it, saying: "The rebel power is at its height; we cannot retreat first — I shall roll up armor and hasten there."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing refused. "The rebels are at their strongest," he said. "We cannot pull back first — I shall march at once."

sentences.zh: 護之曰：「賊謂南州用三萬人，而將軍麾下裁十分之一，若往造賊壘，則虛實露矣。

translations.literal: Huzhi said: "The rebels believe the southern region uses thirty thousand men, while under the General's command there is barely one-tenth; if you go to the rebel camp, truth and falsehood will be exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Huzhi said: "The enemy thinks the south has thirty thousand men, while you command barely a tenth of that. If you go to their camp yourself, our weakness will be exposed.

sentences.zh: 王豫州必不可來，不如分兵援之。」

translations.literal: Governor Wang of Yu Province surely cannot come — better to divide troops to reinforce them."
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wang of Yuzhou certainly cannot come — it would be better to send part of your force to reinforce us."

sentences.zh: 元景曰：「善！」

translations.literal: Yuanjing said: "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing said: "Well said!"

sentences.zh: 乃留贏弱自守，悉遣精兵助玄謨，多張旗幟。

translations.literal: He then left the weak to hold defense and sent all elite troops to aid Xuemo, deploying many banners and flags.
translations.idiomatic: He left the weaker troops to hold his position and sent all his best soldiers to aid Xuemo, with many banners and flags.

sentences.zh: 梁山望之如數萬人，皆以為建康兵悉至，眾心乃安。

translations.literal: From Liangshan they looked like tens of thousands; all thought the Jiankang army had fully arrived, and the troops' hearts were steadied.
translations.idiomatic: Seen from Liangshan, they looked like tens of thousands of men. Everyone thought the full Jiankang army had arrived, and morale steadied.

sentences.zh: 質請自攻東城。

translations.literal: Zhi requested to attack the eastern fort himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi asked to lead the assault on the eastern fort himself.

sentences.zh: 咨議參軍顏樂之說義宣曰：「質若復克東城，則大功盡歸之矣；

translations.literal: Staff Adviser Yan Yuezhi urged Yixuan, saying: "If Zhi again captures the eastern fort, all great merit will go to him;
translations.idiomatic: Staff Adviser Yan Yuezhi told Yixuan: "If Zhi takes the eastern fort again, all the glory will be his;

sentences.zh: 宜遣麾下自行。」

translations.literal: Your own subordinates should be sent to do it."
translations.idiomatic: You should send your own men instead."

sentences.zh: 義宣乃遣劉諶之與質俱進。

translations.literal: Yixuan then sent Liu Chenzhi to advance together with Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan then sent Liu Chenzhi to advance alongside Zhi.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，義宣至梁山，頓兵西岸，質與劉諶之進攻東城。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Yixuan reached Liangshan, encamped on the western bank; Zhi and Liu Chenzhi advanced to attack the eastern fort.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Yixuan reached Liangshan and halted on the western bank while Zhi and Liu Chenzhi pressed the attack on the eastern fort.

sentences.zh: 玄謨督諸軍大戰，薛安都帥突騎先沖其陳之東南，陷之，斬諶之道，劉季之、宗越又陷其西北，質等兵大敗。

translations.literal: Xuemo supervised the armies in a great battle; Xue Andu led shock cavalry to first charge their formation's southeast and break it, cutting down Chenzhi on the road; Liu Jizhi and Zong Yue again broke their northwest; Zhi's army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Xuemo commanded the armies in a great battle. Xue Andu led his shock cavalry in a charge against the southeast of their line and broke through, killing Liu Chenzhi in flight. Liu Jizhi and Zong Yue then broke their northwest flank, and Zhi's army was routed.

sentences.zh: 垣護之燒江中舟艦，煙焰覆水，延及西岸，營壘殆盡；

translations.literal: Yuan Huzhi burned the ships in the river; smoke and flame covered the water, spread to the western bank, and the camps were nearly all consumed;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Huzhi set fire to the ships in the river. Smoke and flame covered the water, spread to the western bank, and nearly all the camps were destroyed;

sentences.zh: 諸軍乘勢攻之，義宣兵亦潰。

translations.literal: The armies pressed the advantage in attack; Yixuan's troops also routed.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial armies pressed the attack, and Yixuan's forces broke and fled as well.

sentences.zh: 義宣單舸迸走，閉戶而泣，荊州人隨之者猶百餘舸。

translations.literal: Yixuan fled alone in a single boat, weeping behind closed doors; Jingzhou men who followed still numbered over a hundred boats.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan fled alone in a single boat, weeping behind closed doors. More than a hundred boats of men from Jingzhou still followed him.

sentences.zh: 質欲見義宣計事，而義宣已去。

translations.literal: Zhi wished to see Yixuan to consult on affairs, but Yixuan had already departed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi wanted to see Yixuan to plan their next move, but Yixuan was already gone.

sentences.zh: 質不知所為，亦走，其眾皆降散。

translations.literal: Zhi did not know what to do and also fled; his host all surrendered and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Not knowing what else to do, Zhi fled too, and his army surrendered and dispersed.

sentences.zh: 己未，解嚴。

translations.literal: On jiwei, martial law was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, the emergency mobilization was lifted.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以吳興太守劉延孫為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On guihai, Liu Yansun, Governor of Wuxing, was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Liu Yansun, governor of Wuxing, was appointed Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙寅，魏主如陰山。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingyin, the Wei ruler went to Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingyin, the Wei emperor traveled to Yinshan.

sentences.zh: 臧質至尋陽，焚燒府捨，載妓妾西走；

translations.literal: Zang Zhi reached Xunyang, burned the government buildings, loaded his courtesans and concubines and fled west;
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi reached Xunyang, burned the government offices, loaded his concubines aboard, and fled west;

sentences.zh: 使嬖人何文敬領餘兵居前，至西陽。

translations.literal: He had his favorite He Wenjing lead the remaining troops ahead, reaching Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his favorite, He Wenjing, ahead with the remaining troops as far as Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 西陽太守魯方平紿文敬曰：「詔書唯捕元惡，餘無所問。

translations.literal: Xiyang Governor Lu Fangping deceived Wenjing, saying: "The imperial edict seeks only the chief villain; the rest are not to be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Fangping, governor of Xiyang, tricked Wenjing, saying: "The edict seeks only the ringleader; no one else is to be pursued.

sentences.zh: 不如逃之。」

translations.literal: Better to flee."
translations.idiomatic: You had better run."

sentences.zh: 文敬棄眾亡去。

translations.literal: Wenjing abandoned his host and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing abandoned his troops and fled.

sentences.zh: 質先以妹夫羊沖為武昌郡，質往投之。

translations.literal: Zhi had previously had his brother-in-law Yang Chong made Administrator of Wuchang; Zhi went to seek refuge with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had earlier had his brother-in-law Yang Chong appointed administrator of Wuchang, and now he went to seek refuge with him.

sentences.zh: 沖已為郡丞胡庇之所殺，質無所歸，乃逃於南湖。

translations.literal: Chong had already been killed by Assistant Administrator Hu Pizhi; Zhi had nowhere to go and fled to Nanhu.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had already been killed by the assistant administrator Hu Pizhi. With nowhere left to turn, Zhi fled to Nanhu.

sentences.zh: 掇蓮實啖之，追兵至，以荷覆頭，自沉於水，出其鼻。

translations.literal: He plucked lotus fruit to eat; when pursuers arrived, he covered his head with lotus leaves, submerged himself in the water, and exposed his nose to breathe.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on lotus seeds. When pursuers came, he covered his head with lotus leaves, sank beneath the water, and left only his nose above the surface to breathe.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，軍主鄭俱兒望見，射之，中心，兵刃亂至，腸胃縈水草，斬首送建康，子孫皆棄市，並誅其黨豫章太守樂安任薈之、臨川內史劉懷之、鄱陽太守杜仲儒。

translations.literal: On wuchen, army commander Zheng Ju'er saw him, shot him, hit the center; weapons fell upon him in confusion; intestines and stomach were tangled with water weeds; his head was cut off and sent to Jiankang; his descendants were all executed in the marketplace; together were executed his partisans Le'an Ren Huizhi, Administrator of Yuzhang, Liu Huaizhi, Interior Secretary of Linchuan, and Du Zhongru, Administrator of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, army commander Zheng Ju'er spotted him and shot him in the chest. Soldiers closed in and hacked him apart; his entrails were tangled with water weeds. His head was sent to Jiankang, his descendants were executed in the marketplace, and his allies were put to death as well: Ren Huizhi of Le'an, administrator of Yuzhang; Liu Huaizhi, interior secretary of Linchuan; and Du Zhongru, administrator of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 仲儒，驥之兄子也。

translations.literal: Zhongru was nephew to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongru was the nephew of Du Ji.

sentences.zh: 功臣柳元景等封賞各有差。

translations.literal: Meritorious officials such as Liu Yuanjing received enfeoffments and rewards in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious officials such as Liu Yuanjing were enfeoffed and rewarded according to their deeds.

sentences.zh: 丞相義宣走至江夏，聞巴陵有軍，回向江陵，眾散且盡，與左右十許人徙走，腳痛不能前，僦民露車自載，緣道求食。

translations.literal: Chancellor Yixuan fled as far as Jiangxia; hearing there were troops at Balin, he turned back toward Jiangling; his host scattered and was nearly gone; with about ten attendants he fled on foot; his feet ached and he could not go forward; he hired a commoner's open cart to carry himself and begged food along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yixuan fled as far as Jiangxia. Hearing that Balin was occupied, he turned back toward Jiangling, but his followers had scattered until almost none remained. With only a dozen or so attendants he went on foot; his feet were too sore to continue, so he hired a peasant's open cart, rode in it, and begged food along the way.

sentences.zh: 至江陵郭外，遣人報竺超民，超民具羽儀兵眾迎之。

translations.literal: Reaching outside Jiangling's walls, he sent someone to notify Zhu Chaomin; Chaomin prepared guards of honor and troops to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the outskirts of Jiangling, he sent word to Zhu Chaomin, who came out with guards of honor and troops to receive him.

sentences.zh: 時荊州帶甲尚萬餘人，左右翟靈寶誡義宣使撫慰將佐，以「臧質違指授之宜，用致失利。

translations.literal: At the time Jingzhou still had over ten thousand armored men; Yixuan's aide Zhai Lingbao admonished him to reassure the officers, saying "Zang Zhi violated proper command and thereby caused defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou still had more than ten thousand armed men. Yixuan's aide Zhai Lingbao urged him to rally his officers, telling them, "Zang Zhi disobeyed orders and brought on our defeat.

sentences.zh: 今治兵繕甲，更為後圖。

translations.literal: Now we shall drill troops and repair armor and plan anew for the future.
translations.idiomatic: Now we must retrain our troops, repair our armor, and plan anew.

sentences.zh: 昔漢高百敗，終成大業！」

translations.literal: In antiquity Gaozu of Han was defeated a hundred times, yet ultimately achieved the great enterprise!"
translations.idiomatic: In old times Gaozu of Han was beaten a hundred times, yet in the end he won the empire!"

sentences.zh: 而義宣忘靈寶之言，誤云「項羽千敗」，眾咸掩口。

translations.literal: But Yixuan forgot Lingbao's words and mistakenly said "Xiang Yu was defeated a thousand times"; the crowd all covered their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: But Yixuan forgot what Lingbao had said and blurted out, "Xiang Yu was defeated a thousand times." The men all stifled their laughter behind their hands.

sentences.zh: 魯秀、竺超民等猶欲收餘兵更圖一決；

translations.literal: Lu Xiu, Zhu Chaomin, and others still wished to gather remnant troops and seek one final decision;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiu, Zhu Chaomin, and others still wanted to gather the remaining troops and fight one last decisive battle;

sentences.zh: 而義宣惛沮，無復神守，入內不復出，左右腹心稍稍離叛。

translations.literal: But Yixuan was dazed and dejected, no longer had spirit to hold himself; he entered within and did not come out again; his close intimates gradually deserted.
translations.idiomatic: But Yixuan was dazed and broken in spirit. He withdrew indoors and would not come out again, and his closest followers gradually deserted him.

sentences.zh: 魯秀北走，義宣不能自立，欲隨秀去，乃攜息慆及所愛妾五人著男子服相隨。

translations.literal: Lu Xiu fled north; Yixuan could not stand on his own and wished to follow Xiu; he then took his son Tao and five beloved concubines in men's dress to go along.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xiu fled north, Yixuan, unable to hold on alone, decided to go with him. He took his son Tao and five favorite concubines, all dressed as men, and set out after him.

sentences.zh: 城內擾亂。

translations.literal: Within the city there was turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 白刃交橫，義宣懼，墜馬，遂步進；

translations.literal: Naked blades crossed everywhere; Yixuan was afraid, fell from his horse, and proceeded on foot;
translations.idiomatic: Blades flashed on every side. Terrified, Yixuan fell from his horse and went on foot;

sentences.zh: 竺超民送至城外，更以馬與之，歸而城守。

translations.literal: Zhu Chaomin escorted him outside the city wall, gave him a horse in exchange, and returned to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Chaomin escorted him beyond the walls, gave him a horse, and returned to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 義宣求秀不得，左右盡棄之，夜，復還南郡空廨；

translations.literal: Yixuan could not find Xiu; his attendants all abandoned him; at night he returned again to the empty yamen of Nan Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Unable to find Lu Xiu and abandoned by his attendants, Yixuan returned by night to the empty offices of Nan Commandery;

sentences.zh: 旦日，超民收送刺奸。

translations.literal: At dawn, Chaomin apprehended him and sent him to the Office of Investigation.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, Chaomin seized him and handed him over to the cijian office.

sentences.zh: 義宣止獄戶，坐地歎曰：「臧質老奴誤我！」

translations.literal: Yixuan stopped at the prison gate, sat on the ground and sighed, saying: "That old scoundrel Zang Zhi has ruined me!"
translations.idiomatic: At the prison gate Yixuan sat down on the ground and sighed: "That old villain Zang Zhi has ruined me!"

sentences.zh: 五妾尋被遣出，義宣號泣，語獄吏曰：「常日非苦，今日分別始是苦。」

translations.literal: Soon the five concubines were sent out; Yixuan wailed and wept and told the prison officer: "Ordinary days were not bitter; today's parting is when bitterness begins."
translations.idiomatic: Soon his five concubines were sent away. Yixuan wept aloud and told the jailer: "Life had not been hard before; only now, at this parting, does the pain begin."

sentences.zh: 魯秀眾散，不能去，還向江陵，城上人射之，秀赴水死，就取其首。

translations.literal: Lu Xiu's host scattered; unable to leave, he turned back toward Jiangling; men on the wall shot at him; Xiu threw himself into the water and died; they took his head.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiu's followers had scattered. Unable to escape, he turned back toward Jiangling, but men on the walls shot at him. He threw himself into the river and drowned, and they took his head.

sentences.zh: 詔右僕射劉延孫使荊、江二州，旌別枉直，就行誅賞；

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Right Vice Director Liu Yansun to the two provinces of Jing and Jiang to distinguish wrong from right and carry out punishments and rewards on the spot;
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Right Vice Director Liu Yansun to Jing and Jiang to judge right and wrong and carry out punishments and rewards on the spot;

sentences.zh: 且分割二州之地，議更置新州。

translations.literal: and also to divide the territory of the two provinces and discuss establishing new provinces.
translations.idiomatic: and also to partition their territories and consider creating new provinces.

sentences.zh: 初，晉氏南遷，以揚州為京畿，谷帛所資皆出焉；

translations.literal: Initially, when the Jin house moved south, they made Yang Province the capital region; grain and cloth supplies all came from it;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Jin court moved south, it made Yang Province the capital region, and grain and cloth for the court all came from there;

sentences.zh: 以荊、江為重鎮，甲兵所聚盡在焉，常使大將居之。

translations.literal: Jing and Jiang were made key strongholds; gathered armor and troops were all there; a great general was usually stationed there.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Jiang were treated as major strongholds where armor and troops were concentrated, and a senior general was usually posted there.

sentences.zh: 三州戶口，居江南之半，上惡其強大，故欲分之。

translations.literal: The three provinces' registered households constituted half of south of the Yangzi; the Emperor hated their great strength and therefore wished to divide them.
translations.idiomatic: Together these three provinces held half the registered population south of the Yangzi. The emperor resented their power and therefore wanted to break them up.

sentences.zh: 癸未，分揚州浙東五郡置東揚州，治會稽；

translations.literal: On guiwei, five commanderies of eastern Zhejiang were split from Yang Province to establish Eastern Yang Province, administered from Kuaiji;
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, five commanderies in eastern Zhejiang were split off from Yang Province to form Eastern Yang Province, with its seat at Kuaiji;

sentences.zh: 分荊、湘、江、豫州之八郡置郢州，治江夏；

translations.literal: eight commanderies from Jing, Xiang, Jiang, and Yu provinces were split to establish Ying Province, administered from Jiangxia;
translations.idiomatic: eight commanderies from Jing, Xiang, Jiang, and Yu were carved out to form Ying Province, with its seat at Jiangxia;

sentences.zh: 罷南蠻校尉，遷其營於建康。

translations.literal: The Commandant of Southern Man was abolished and his camp moved to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant of Southern Man was abolished, and his garrison was moved to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 太傅義恭議使郢州治巴陵，尚書令何尚之曰：「夏口在荊、江之中，正對沔口，通接雍、梁，實為津要。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yigong proposed making Ying Province's seat at Balin; Minister He Shangzhi said: "Xiakou lies between Jing and Jiang, directly facing the Han River mouth, connecting Yong and Liang — it is truly a strategic ford.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yigong proposed placing Ying Province's capital at Balin, but Minister He Shangzhi said: "Xiakou lies between Jing and Jiang, directly opposite the mouth of the Han, and links Yong and Liang. It is truly a vital crossing.

sentences.zh: 由來舊鎮，根基不易，既有見城，浦大容舫，於是為便。」

translations.literal: It has long been an old stronghold with roots not easily moved; there is already an existing city; the harbor is large enough for ships — thereby it is convenient."
translations.idiomatic: It has long been an established stronghold whose foundations should not be lightly moved. There is already a walled city there, and the harbor is broad enough for large ships — that makes it the better choice."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 既而荊、揚因此虛耗，尚之請復合二州，上不許。

translations.literal: Afterward Jing and Yang were thereby weakened; Shangzhi requested reuniting the two provinces, but the Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Jing and Yang were weakened by the division. Shangzhi asked that the two provinces be reunited, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 戊子，省錄尚書事。

translations.literal: On wuzi, the post of Supervisor of Affairs of the Masters of Writing was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, the office of Supervisor of the Masters of Writing was abolished.

sentences.zh: 上惡宗室強盛，不欲權在臣下；

translations.literal: The Emperor hated that the imperial clan was powerful and did not wish authority to rest with subjects below;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor resented the power of the imperial clan and did not want authority to remain in the hands of his ministers;

sentences.zh: 太傅義恭知其指，故請省之。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yigong understood his intent and therefore requested its abolition.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yigong understood what he wanted and therefore asked that the office be abolished.

sentences.zh: 上使王公、八座與荊州刺史朱修之書，令丞相義宣自為計。

translations.literal: The Emperor had the princes and dukes and the Eight Counselors write to Jing Province Governor Zhu Xiuzhi, ordering Chancellor Yixuan to take counsel for himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the princes and dukes and the Eight Counselors write to Zhu Xiuzhi, governor of Jing Province, instructing Chancellor Yixuan to decide his own fate.

sentences.zh: 書未達，庚寅，修之入江陵，殺義宣，並誅其子十六人，及同黨竺超民、從事中郎蔡超、咨議參軍顏樂之等。

translations.literal: Before the letter arrived, on gengyin, Xiuzhi entered Jiangling, killed Yixuan, and executed his sixteen sons together with co-conspirators Zhu Chaomin, Attendant-in-Ordinary Cai Chao, Staff Adviser Yan Yuezhi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Before the letter arrived, on gengyin, Xiuzhi entered Jiangling, killed Yixuan, and executed his sixteen sons, along with his co-conspirators Zhu Chaomin, Attendant-in-Ordinary Cai Chao, Staff Adviser Yan Yuezhi, and others.

sentences.zh: 超民兄弟應從誅，何尚之上言：「賊既遁走，一夫可擒。

translations.literal: Chaomin's brothers ought to be executed with him; He Shangzhi memorialized: "The rebels having fled, a single man can be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Chaomin's brothers deserved to die with him, but He Shangzhi memorialized: "The rebels have fled; one man can be taken.

sentences.zh: 若超民反覆昧利，即當取之，非唯免愆，亦可要不義之賞。

translations.literal: If Chaomin were to turn and scheme for profit, then one ought seize him — not only escaping guilt but also extracting an unrighteous reward.
translations.idiomatic: If Chaomin had turned treacherous for gain, he should have been seized — not only to escape blame but to claim an ill-gotten reward.

sentences.zh: 而超民曾無此意，微足觀過知仁。

translations.literal: Yet Chaomin never had such intent; it is enough, in small measure, to observe fault and know benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chaomin never harbored such intent — enough, in small measure, to read his fault and see his virtue.

sentences.zh: 且為官保全城府，謹守庫藏，端坐待縛。

translations.literal: Moreover he preserved the city walls and moat on behalf of the government, guarded the treasuries carefully, and sat upright awaiting binding.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he had preserved the city on the state's behalf, guarded the storehouses, and sat waiting to be bound.

sentences.zh: 今戮及兄弟，則與其餘逆黨無異，於事為重。」

translations.literal: Now if execution extends to his brothers, they will be no different from the other rebel partisans — a weighty matter for affairs of state."
translations.idiomatic: If his brothers are executed too, they will be treated no differently from the other rebels — a grave matter for policy."

sentences.zh: 上乃原之。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙申朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day of the month (bingchen), there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day bingchen, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 庚子，魏皇子弘生；

translations.literal: On gengzi, the Wei emperor's son Hong was born;
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, the Wei emperor's son Hong was born;

sentences.zh: 辛丑，大赦，改元興光。

translations.literal: on xinchou, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Xingguang.
translations.idiomatic: on xinchou, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed to Xingguang.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，大赦。

translations.literal: On bingchen, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲戌，魏趙王深卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiaxu, Zhao Wang Shen of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiaxu, Zhao Wang Shen of Wei died.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: On yihai, the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，戊戌，魏主如中山，遂如信都；

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on wuxu, the Wei emperor went to Zhongshan, then to Xindu;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on wuxu, the Wei emperor went to Zhongshan, then to Xindu;

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙子，還，幸靈丘，至溫泉宮；

translations.literal: in the twelfth month, on bingzi, he returned, visited Lingqiu, and reached the Hot Springs Palace;
translations.idiomatic: in the twelfth month, on bingzi, he returned, visited Lingqiu, and reached the Hot Springs Palace;

sentences.zh: 庚辰，還平城。

translations.literal: on gengchen, he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: on gengchen, he returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝武皇帝上孝建二年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu the Founding Ancestor, upper fascicle — second year of Xiaojian (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu, upper fascicle — the second year of Xiaojian (

sentences.zh: 乙未，公元四五五年）

translations.literal: yiwei, the year 455 CE)
translations.idiomatic: yiwei, 455 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，魏車騎大將軍樂平王拔有罪，賜死。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the Wei General of Chariots and Cavalry, Prince of Le Ping Ba, was guilty and was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the Wei General of Chariots and Cavalry, Prince of Le Ping Ba, was found guilty and ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 鎮北大將軍、南兗州刺史沈慶之請老；

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Southern Yan Province Shen Qingzhi requested retirement;
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Southern Yan Province Shen Qingzhi asked to retire;

sentences.zh: 二月，丙寅，以為左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: in the second month, on bingyin, he was made Left Master of Splendid Happiness with Office Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: in the second month, on bingyin, he was made Left Master of Splendid Happiness with Office Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 慶之固讓，表疏數十上，又面自陳，乃至稽顙泣涕。

translations.literal: Qingzhi firmly declined; he submitted memorials dozens of times, also pleaded face to face, even prostrating himself with tears.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi refused firmly, submitting memorial after memorial and pleading in person, even kowtowing with tears.

sentences.zh: 上不能奪，聽以始興公就第，厚加給奉。

translations.literal: The Emperor could not override him and permitted him to retire to his estate as Duke of Shixing, with generous stipends.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not change his mind and let him retire to his estate as Duke of Shixing, with generous allowances.

sentences.zh: 頃之，上復欲用慶之，使何尚之往起之。

translations.literal: Before long, the Emperor again wished to employ Qingzhi and sent He Shangzhi to summon him back.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, the emperor again wanted to use Qingzhi and sent He Shangzhi to bring him back.

sentences.zh: 尚之累陳上意，慶之笑曰：「沈公不效何公，往而復返。」

translations.literal: Shangzhi repeatedly conveyed the Emperor's intent; Qingzhi laughed and said: "Lord Shen is not like Lord He — going and returning again."
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi repeated the emperor's wishes, but Qingzhi laughed and said, "Lord Shen is not Lord He — I do not go out and come back again."

sentences.zh: 尚之慚而止。

translations.literal: Shangzhi, ashamed, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi, ashamed, gave up.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以尚書右僕射劉延孫為南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Liu Yansun, Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, was made Governor of Southern Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Liu Yansun, Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, was made Governor of Southern Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，戊戌，以湘州刺史劉遵考為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on wuxu, Liu Zunkao, Governor of Xiang Province, was made Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on wuxu, Liu Zunkao, Governor of Xiang Province, was made Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬戌，魏改元太安。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renxu, Wei changed the era name to Taian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renxu, Wei changed the era name to Taian.

sentences.zh: 甲子，大赦。

translations.literal: On jiazi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 甲申，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸巳，立皇弟休祐為山陽王，休茂為海陵王，休業為鄱陽王。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on guisi, the Emperor's younger brother Xiuyou was established as Prince of Shanyang, Xiumao as Prince of Hailing, and Xiuye as Prince of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on guisi, the emperor's younger brothers Xiuyou, Xiumao, and Xiuye were made Princes of Shanyang, Hailing, and Poyang.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，魏主如河西。

translations.literal: On bingchen, the Wei emperor went to Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, the Wei emperor went to Hexi.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史武昌王渾與左右作檄文，自號楚王，改元永光，備置百官，以為戲笑。

translations.literal: Governor of Yong Province, Prince of Wuchang Hun, with his attendants drafted a proclamation, styled himself King of Chu, changed the era name to Yongguang, fully set up officials — all as jest and mockery.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wuchang Hun, Governor of Yong Province, drafted a proclamation with his attendants, styled himself King of Chu, changed the era name to Yongguang, and set up a full roster of officials — all in jest.

sentences.zh: 長史王翼之封呈其手跡。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Wang Yizhi sealed and submitted his handwriting.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Wang Yizhi sealed and forwarded his handwriting.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚申，廢渾為庶人，徙始安郡。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on gengshen, Hun was deposed as a commoner and moved to Shian Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengshen, Hun was deposed to commoner status and exiled to Shian Commandery.

sentences.zh: 上遣員外散騎侍郎東海戴明寶詰責渾，因逼令自殺，時年十七。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Without Regular Appointment Dai Mingbao of Donghai to rebuke Hun and compelled him to take his own life; he was then seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Without Regular Appointment Dai Mingbao of Donghai to rebuke Hun and forced him to kill himself; he was seventeen.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 詔祀郊廟，初設備樂，從前殿中曹郎荀萬秋之議也。

translations.literal: An edict ordered sacrifice at the suburban altars and temples; ritual music was established for the first time — following the proposal of Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Front Hall Xun Wanqiu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered sacrifices at the suburban altars and temples; full ritual music was established for the first time, following the proposal of Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Front Hall Xun Wanqiu.

sentences.zh: 上欲削弱王侯。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to weaken kings and marquises.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to weaken the power of kings and marquises.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己未，江夏王義恭、竟陵王誕奏裁損王、侯車服、器用、樂舞制度，凡九事；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiwei, Liu Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, and Liu Dan, Prince of Jingling, memorialized cutting back princes' and marquises' chariots, dress, utensils, music, and dance regulations — nine items in all;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiwei, Liu Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, and Liu Dan, Prince of Jingling, memorialized nine cuts to princes' and marquises' chariots, dress, utensils, music, and dance;

sentences.zh: 上因諷有司奏增廣為二十四條，聽事不得南向坐，施帳；

translations.literal: the Emperor, through indirect suggestion, had the relevant offices memorialize expanding this to twenty-four articles: audience halls might not face south for seating, nor have canopies erected;
translations.idiomatic: the emperor then prompted the offices to expand the list to twenty-four articles: princes might not sit facing south in their audience halls or erect canopies;

sentences.zh: 劍不得為鹿盧形；

translations.literal: swords might not be in deer-antler form;
translations.idiomatic: swords might not take the deer-antler shape;

sentences.zh: 內史、相及封內官長止稱下官，不得稱臣，罷官則不復追敬。

translations.literal: interior stewards, chancellors, and senior officials within fiefs might only style themselves "subordinate officer," not "your subject"; once dismissed from office they would no longer be paid formal respect.
translations.idiomatic: interior stewards, chancellors, and senior officials within fiefs might only call themselves "subordinate officer," not "your subject," and once dismissed would no longer receive formal homage.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was approved.

sentences.zh: 庚午，魏以遼西王常英為太宰。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Wei made Chang Ying, Prince of Liaoxi, Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Wei made Chang Ying, Prince of Liaoxi, Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以太傅義恭領揚州刺史，竟陵王誕為司空、領南徐州刺史，建平王寵為尚書令。

translations.literal: On renwu, Grand Tutor Yigong was made concurrent Governor of Yang Province; Prince of Jingling Dan was made Minister of Works and concurrent Governor of Southern Xu Province; Prince of Jianping Chong was made Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Grand Tutor Yigong took charge of Yang Province; Prince of Jingling Dan was made Minister of Works and concurrent Governor of Southern Xu Province; Prince of Jianping Chong was made Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以故氐王楊保宗子元和為征虜將軍，楊頭為輔國將軍。

translations.literal: That year, Yuanhe, son of the former Di king Yang Baozong, was made General Who Subdues the Barbarians; Yang Tou was made General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Yuanhe, son of the former Di king Yang Baozong, was made General Who Subdues the Barbarians, and Yang Tou was made General Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 頭，文德之從祖兄也。

translations.literal: Tou was a paternal cousin once removed of Wendé.
translations.idiomatic: Tou was Wendé's first cousin once removed.

sentences.zh: 元和雖楊氏正統，朝廷以其年幼才弱，未正位號，部落無定主，頭先戍葭蘆，母妻子弟並為魏所執，而頭為宋堅守無貳心。

translations.literal: Though Yuanhe was the legitimate Yang line, the court, because he was young and weak in talent, had not confirmed his rank and title; the tribe had no settled chief. Tou had first garrisoned Jialu; his mother, wife, children, and younger brothers were all seized by Wei, yet Tou held firm for Song without disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yuanhe was the legitimate Yang heir, the court had not confirmed his rank because he was young and untested, and the tribe had no settled leader. Tou had garrisoned Jialu first; Wei held his mother, wife, children, and brothers, yet he remained loyal to Song.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史王玄謨上言：「請以頭為假節、西秦州刺史，用安輯其眾。

translations.literal: Governor of Yong Province Wang Xuemo memorialized: "I request that Tou be made Acting Credential Bearer and Governor of Western Qin, to pacify and settle the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Yong Province Wang Xuemo memorialized: "I ask that Tou be made Acting Credential Bearer and Governor of Western Qin to pacify the people.

sentences.zh: 俟數年之後，元和稍長，使嗣故業。

translations.literal: After several years, when Yuanhe has grown somewhat, let him succeed to the former domain.
translations.idiomatic: After a few years, when Yuanhe has matured, let him succeed to the old domain.

sentences.zh: 若元和才用不稱，便應歸頭，頭能籓扞漢川，使無虜患，彼四千戶荒州殆不足惜。

translations.literal: If Yuanhe's talent and capacity do not fit, then power should revert to Tou. Tou can screen and defend the Han River basin and keep it free of barbarian trouble — that desolate province of four thousand households is scarcely worth regretting.
translations.idiomatic: If Yuanhe proves unfit, power should return to Tou. Tou can shield the Han River basin from the enemy; that barren province of four thousand households is hardly worth keeping.

sentences.zh: 若葭蘆不守，漢川亦無立理。」

translations.literal: If Jialu is not held, the Han River basin has no basis to stand on either."
translations.idiomatic: If Jialu falls, the Han River basin cannot stand either."

sentences.zh: 上不從。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not follow the advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝武皇帝上孝建三年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu the Founding Ancestor, upper fascicle — third year of Xiaojian (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu, upper fascicle — the third year of Xiaojian (

sentences.zh: 丙申，公元四五六年）

translations.literal: bingshen, the year 456 CE)
translations.idiomatic: bingshen, 456 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚寅，立皇弟休范為順陽王，休若為巴陵王。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on gengyin, the Emperor's younger brothers Xiufan and Xioruo were established as Princes of Shunyang and Baling.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on gengyin, the emperor's younger brothers Xiufan and Xioruo were made Princes of Shunyang and Baling.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，立皇子子尚為西陽王。

translations.literal: On wuxu, the imperial son Zishang was established as Prince of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, the imperial son Zishang was made Prince of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 壬子，納右衛將軍何瑀女為太子妃。

translations.literal: On renzi, the daughter of He Yu, Right Defender General, was taken in marriage as crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, the daughter of Right Defender General He Yu was taken in marriage as crown princess.

sentences.zh: 瑀，澄之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Yu was a great-grandson of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was a great-grandson of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，大赦。

translations.literal: On jiayin, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，魏立貴人馮氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On yimao, Wei established Palace Woman Feng as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Wei established Palace Woman Feng as empress.

sentences.zh: 後，遼西郡公朗之女也；

translations.literal: The Empress was daughter of Duke of Liaoxi Lang;
translations.idiomatic: The empress was the daughter of Duke of Liaoxi Lang;

sentences.zh: 朗為秦、雍二州刺史，坐事誅，後由是沒入宮。

translations.literal: Lang was Governor of Qin and Yong provinces, executed for an offense; the Empress was therefore absorbed into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Lang had been Governor of Qin and Yong provinces and was executed for an offense; she was therefore taken into the palace.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁巳，魏主立子弘為皇太子，先使其母李貴人條記所付託兄弟，然後依故事賜死。

translations.literal: In the second month, on dingsi, the Wei emperor established his son Hong as crown prince; first he had Hong's mother, Lady Li the Palace Woman, itemize in writing the brothers to whom she entrusted her affairs, then, following precedent, she was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on dingsi, the Wei emperor made his son Hong crown prince; first he had Hong's mother, Lady Li, write down the brothers she entrusted with her affairs, then, by precedent, ordered her to die.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以廣州刺史宗愨為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Zong Que, Governor of Guang Province, was made Governor of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Zong Que, Governor of Guang Province, was made Governor of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 故事，府州部內論事，皆簽前直敘所論之事，置典簽以主之。

translations.literal: By precedent, when matters within a prefecture or province were discussed, the subject was stated directly on the endorsement in front; a chief secretary was appointed to manage this.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, provincial business was endorsed with a direct statement of the matter at hand, and a chief secretary was appointed to manage it.

sentences.zh: 宋世諸皇子為方鎮者多幼，時主皆以親近左右領典簽，典簽之權稍重。

translations.literal: In the Song, many imperial sons holding regional commands were young; the reigning sovereigns all put close attendants in charge of the chief secretary post, and the chief secretary's power gradually grew weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song, many imperial sons sent to regional commands were young, and reigning emperors put trusted attendants in charge as chief secretaries, gradually increasing their power.

sentences.zh: 至是，雖長王臨籓，素族出鎮，典簽皆出納教命，執其樞要，刺史不得專其職任。

translations.literal: By this time, even when mature princes held fiefs and common clansmen went out to command, chief secretaries issued and received orders and held the key levers; governors could not monopolize their duties.
translations.idiomatic: By then, even when mature princes held fiefs or common clansmen took command, chief secretaries issued orders and held the levers of power, and governors could not govern alone.

sentences.zh: 及愨為豫州，臨安吳喜為典簽。
