translations.literal: When Que became Governor of Yu Province, Wu Xi of Lin'an was chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Que became Governor of Yu Province, Wu Xi of Lin'an served as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 愨刑政所施，喜每多違執，愨大怒，曰：「宗愨年將六十，為國竭命，正得一州如斗大，不能復與典簽共臨之！」

translations.literal: In the punishments and administration Que imposed, Xi often obstructed contrary to orders; Que grew furious and said: "Zong Que is nearly sixty, having exhausted his life for the state, and has gotten only a province the size of a dipper — I cannot again share its governance with a chief secretary!"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Que imposed punishments or policy, Xi often blocked him. Que flew into a rage and said, "Zong Que is nearly sixty and has spent his life serving the state, yet all he gets is a province the size of a dipper — I will not share its rule with a chief secretary!"

sentences.zh: 喜稽顙流血，乃止。

translations.literal: Xi prostrated himself until he bled and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xi kowtowed until he bled, and Que relented.

sentences.zh: 丁零數千家匿井陘山中為盜，魏選部尚書陸真與州郡合兵討滅之。

translations.literal: Several thousand Dingling families hid in the Jingxing mountains as bandits; Lu Zhen of Wei, Minister of the Bureau of Selection, joined forces with the province and commandery to attack and destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand Dingling families hid in the Jingxing mountains as bandits; Wei's Minister of the Bureau of Selection Lu Zhen joined provincial and commandery troops to attack and wipe them out.

sentences.zh: 閏月，戊午，以尚書左僕射劉遵考為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on wuwu, Liu Zunkao, Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, was made Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on wuwu, Liu Zunkao, Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, was made Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，鄱陽哀王休業卒。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Liu Xiuye, Lamented Prince of Poyang, died.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Liu Xiuye, Lamented Prince of Poyang, died.

sentences.zh: 太傅義恭以南兗州刺史西陽王子尚有寵，將避之，乃辭揚州。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yigong, because Zishang, Prince of Xiyang and Governor of Southern Yan Province, was favored, wished to avoid him and therefore resigned Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yigong, seeing that Zishang, Prince of Xiyang and Governor of Southern Yan Province, was favored, wished to avoid him and resigned Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，解義恭揚州；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Yigong was relieved of Yang Province;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Yigong was relieved of Yang Province;

sentences.zh: 丙子，以子尚為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: on bingzi, Zishang was made Governor of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: on bingzi, Zishang was made Governor of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 時熒惑守南斗，上廢西州舊館，使子尚移治東城以厭之。

translations.literal: At the time Mars held the Southern Dipper; the Emperor abolished the old Western Quarter residence and had Zishang move his seat to the Eastern City to counter the omen.
translations.idiomatic: Mars was then in the Southern Dipper; the emperor abolished the old Western Quarter residence and had Zishang move his seat to the Eastern City to counter the omen.

sentences.zh: 揚州別駕從事沈懷文曰：「天道示變，宜應之以德。」

translations.literal: Shen Huaiwen, Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Governor of Yang Province, said: "Heaven shows a change — one should respond with virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaiwen, Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Governor of Yang Province, said, "Heaven shows a change; one should answer with virtue."

sentences.zh: 今雖空西州，恐無益也。」

translations.literal: Though the Western Quarter is now emptied, I fear it will do no good."
translations.idiomatic: Emptying the Western Quarter will do no good."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not follow the advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 懷文，懷遠之兄也。

translations.literal: Huaiwen was elder brother to Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen was the elder brother of Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 八月，魏平西將軍漁陽公尉眷擊伊吾，克其城，大獲而還。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Yu Juan, Duke of Yuyang and General Who Pacifies the West of Wei, attacked Yiwu, captured its city, and returned with great booty.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Yu Juan, Duke of Yuyang and General Who Pacifies the West of Wei, attacked Yiwu, took the city, and returned with great booty.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬戌，以丹陽尹劉遵考為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on renxu, Liu Zunkao, Governor of Danyang, was made Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renxu, Liu Zunkao, Governor of Danyang, was made Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲申，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiashen, the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiashen, the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 丙午，太傅義恭進位太宰，領司徒。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Grand Tutor Yigong was promoted to Grand Preceptor and made concurrent Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Grand Tutor Yigong was promoted to Grand Preceptor and made concurrent Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 十一月，魏以尚書西平王源賀為冀州刺史，更賜爵隴西王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Wei made Wang Yuanhe of Xiping, Minister of the Masters of Writing, Governor of Ji Province, and further granted the title Prince of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Wei made Wang Yuanhe of Xiping, Minister of the Masters of Writing, Governor of Ji Province, and further ennobled him as Prince of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 賀上言：「今北虜遊魂，南寇負險，疆場之間，猶須防戍。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Now the northern barbarians are wandering spirits; the southern enemy holds perilous ground. Between the borders, garrison defense is still needed.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The northern enemy still roams; the southern foe holds difficult ground. The frontier still needs garrisons.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為，自非大逆、赤手殺人，其坐贓盜及過誤應入死者，皆可原宥，謫使守邊；

translations.literal: I humbly believe that except for great treason and bare-handed killing, those convicted of embezzlement, theft, and negligent errors deserving death may all be pardoned and sent to garrison the frontiers;
translations.idiomatic: I believe that except for great treason and bare-handed murder, those condemned to death for embezzlement, theft, or negligent crime should all be pardoned and sent to guard the frontier;

sentences.zh: 則是已斷之體受更生之恩，徭役之家蒙休息之惠。」

translations.literal: then those whose bodies were already forfeit would receive the grace of renewed life, and households bearing corvée labor would enjoy the benefit of rest."
translations.idiomatic: then men already marked for death would receive new life, and corvée households would gain relief."

sentences.zh: 魏高宗從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong of Wei followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng of Wei agreed.

sentences.zh: 久之，謂群臣曰：「吾用賀言，一歲所活不少，增戍兵亦多。

translations.literal: After some time, he told the officials: "Using He's advice, within a year many were spared alive, and frontier garrison troops also increased greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later he told his ministers, "Following He's advice, I spared many lives within the year and added many frontier troops.

sentences.zh: 卿等人人如賀，朕何憂哉！」

translations.literal: If every one of you were like He, what would I have to worry about!
translations.idiomatic: If every one of you were like He, what would I have to fear!

sentences.zh: 會武邑人石華告賀謀反，有司以聞，帝曰：「賀竭誠事國，朕為卿等保之，無此明矣。」

translations.literal: When Shihua of Wuyi reported He for plotting rebellion, the offices reported it; the Emperor said: "He serves the state with all loyalty — I vouch for him before you; this could not be clearer."
translations.idiomatic: When Shihua of Wuyi accused He of rebellion, the offices reported it; the emperor said, "He serves the state with complete loyalty — I vouch for him to you all; nothing could be clearer."

sentences.zh: 命精加訊驗。

translations.literal: He ordered meticulous inquiry and verification.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a thorough investigation.

sentences.zh: 華果引誣，帝誅之，因謂左右曰：「以賀忠誠，猶不免誣謗，不及賀者可無慎哉！」

translations.literal: Shihua indeed confessed to false accusation; the Emperor executed him and then said to those around him: "Even with He's loyalty, he still could not escape slander — those who fall short of He ought to be no less careful!"
translations.idiomatic: Shihua confessed to false accusation; the emperor executed him and told those around him, "Even a man as loyal as He cannot escape slander — how much more should the rest of you be on your guard!"

sentences.zh: 十二月，濮陽太守姜龍駒、新平太守楊自倫帥吏民棄郡奔魏。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Jiang Longju, Governor of Puyang, and Yang Zilun, Governor of Xinping, led officials and people to abandon their commanderies and flee to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Jiang Longju, Governor of Puyang, and Yang Zilun, Governor of Xinping, led officials and people to abandon their commanderies and defect to Wei.

sentences.zh: 上欲移青、冀二州並鎮歷城，議者多不同。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to move Qing and Ji provinces together to garrison Licheng; many in the deliberation disagreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to consolidate Qing and Ji provinces and garrison them at Licheng, but many advisers disagreed.

sentences.zh: 青、冀二州刺史垣護之曰：「青州北有河、濟，又多陂澤，非虜所向；

translations.literal: The Governors of Qing and Ji Provinces, Yuan Huzhi, said: "North of Qing Province are the Yellow and Ji Rivers, and there are many marshes and lakes — not where the barbarians tend to go;
translations.idiomatic: The governors of Qing and Ji provinces, Yuan Huzhi, said: "North of Qing Province lie the Yellow and Ji Rivers, with marshes and lakes throughout — not terrain the northerners favor;

sentences.zh: 每來寇掠，必由歷城。

translations.literal: Each time they come to raid and plunder, they must pass through Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they raid, they must pass through Licheng.

sentences.zh: 二州並鎮，此經遠之略也。

translations.literal: Garrisoning both provinces together — this is the strategy of managing both near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisoning both provinces at one post is the proper strategy for securing both the near frontier and the far.

sentences.zh: 北又近河，歸順者易。

translations.literal: To the north it is also close to the river — those who submit are easily accommodated.
translations.idiomatic: The north is also close to the river, making it easy for defectors to come over.

sentences.zh: 近息民患，遠申王威，安邊之上計也。」

translations.literal: Near at hand, the people's troubles are eased; far off, royal majesty is displayed — the supreme plan for securing the border."
translations.idiomatic: It would ease the people's burdens nearby and project imperial power afar — the best plan for securing the frontier."

sentences.zh: 由是遂定。

translations.literal: Thereupon the matter was settled.
translations.idiomatic: On this basis the decision was made.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，官鑄四銖錢，輪郭、形制與五銖同，用費無利，故民不盜鑄。

translations.literal: During the Yuanjia era, the government cast four-zhu coins; rim and form matched the five-zhu, and production costs yielded no profit, so the people did not counterfeit.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanjia era, the government minted four-zhu coins identical in rim and shape to the five-zhu; production was unprofitable, so private counterfeiting did not occur.

sentences.zh: 及上即位，又鑄孝建四銖，形式薄小，輪郭不成。

translations.literal: When the Emperor ascended the throne, he also cast Xiaojian four-zhu coins — thin and small in form, with rims incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's accession, he minted Xiaojian four-zhu coins — thin, small, and poorly rimmed.

sentences.zh: 於是盜鑄者眾，雜以鉛、錫；

translations.literal: Thereupon counterfeiters were many, mixing in lead and tin;
translations.idiomatic: Counterfeiters proliferated, adulterating coins with lead and tin;

sentences.zh: 翦鑿古錢，錢轉薄小。

translations.literal: they clipped and filed old coins, and money grew ever thinner and smaller.
translations.idiomatic: and clipped and filed old coins until currency grew progressively debased.

sentences.zh: 守宰不能禁，坐死、免者相繼。

translations.literal: Local officials could not prohibit it; those punished by death or dismissal followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Local magistrates could not stop it; officials were executed or dismissed in succession.

sentences.zh: 盜鑄益甚，物價踴貴，朝廷患之。

translations.literal: Counterfeiting grew worse still, and prices surged — the court was troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: Counterfeiting worsened, prices soared, and the court grew alarmed.

sentences.zh: 去歲春，詔錢薄小無輪郭者悉不得行，民間喧擾。

translations.literal: Last spring, an edict declared that thin, small coins without rims could not circulate at all; popular uproar ensued.
translations.idiomatic: The previous spring, an edict banned all thin, rimless coins from circulation, throwing the populace into uproar.

sentences.zh: 是歲，始興郡公沈慶之建議，以為：「宜聽民鑄錢，郡縣置錢署，樂鑄之家皆居署內，平其准式，去其雜偽。

translations.literal: That year, Duke of Shixing Commandery Shen Qingzhi proposed: "It is fitting to permit the people to cast coins; counties and commanderies should establish mint offices, and families willing to cast should all reside within the offices, standardizing specifications and eliminating adulteration and forgery.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Shen Qingzhi, Duke of Shixing Commandery, proposed: "Let the people mint coins under government oversight — each county should establish a mint office where private minters would reside, with standardized weights and purity to eliminate fraud.

sentences.zh: 去春所禁新品，一時施用，今鑄悉依此格。

translations.literal: The new coins banned last spring should be put into use all at once; all casting now should follow this standard.
translations.idiomatic: The new coins banned last spring should be released immediately, and all new minting should follow this standard.

sentences.zh: 萬稅三千，嚴檢盜鑄。」

translations.literal: Of every ten thousand, tax three thousand; strictly inspect for counterfeiting."
translations.idiomatic: Impose a tax of three thousand per ten thousand coins minted, and strictly suppress illicit casting."

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹顏竣駁之，以為：「五銖輕重，定於漢世，魏、晉以降，莫之能改；

translations.literal: Danyang Intendant Yan Jun rebutted him, arguing: "The weight of the five-zhu was fixed in the Han dynasty; from Wei and Jin downward, none could alter it;
translations.idiomatic: Danyang Intendant Yan Jun objected: "The five-zhu standard was set in Han times, and from Wei and Jin onward no one has changed it —

sentences.zh: 誠以物貨既均，改之偽生故也。

translations.literal: truly because goods and currency were already balanced, and changing it would breed forgery.
translations.idiomatic: precisely because the currency was stable; altering it only invites fraud.

sentences.zh: 今雲去春所禁一時施用；

translations.literal: Now you say the coins banned last spring should be put into use all at once;
translations.idiomatic: Now you propose releasing last spring's banned coins all at once;

sentences.zh: 若鉅細總行而不從公鑄，利己既深，情偽無極，私鑄、翦鑿盡不可禁，財華未贍，大錢已竭，數歲之間，悉為塵土矣。

translations.literal: if large and small all circulate together without following public minting, private profit runs deep, deceit knows no limit, private casting and clipping cannot be prohibited at all — wealth will not suffice, large coins will be exhausted, and within a few years all will be reduced to dust.
translations.idiomatic: if debased coins of every size circulate without strict public minting, private gain will run rampant, fraud will know no bounds, and clipping and counterfeiting will become unstoppable — treasury reserves will not cover the loss, large coins will vanish, and within a few years the currency will be worthless.

sentences.zh: 今新禁初行，品式未一，須臾自止，不足以垂聖慮；

translations.literal: Now the new prohibition has only just begun; types and standards are not yet uniform — in a moment it will stop on its own; this is not enough to bear upon imperial concern;
translations.idiomatic: The new ban has only just begun; standards are not yet uniform, and turmoil will soon subside on its own — this hardly warrants imperial intervention;

sentences.zh: 唯府藏空匱，實為重憂。

translations.literal: only that the treasury stores are empty — this is truly a grave worry.
translations.idiomatic: only the empty treasury is a genuine and pressing concern.

sentences.zh: 今縱行細錢，官無益賦之理；

translations.literal: Now even if small coins are allowed to circulate, the government has no basis for increased revenue;
translations.idiomatic: Even if small coins circulate freely, the state gains no additional revenue;

sentences.zh: 百姓雖贍，無解官乏。

translations.literal: though the common people may be supplied, it does not resolve the government's want.
translations.idiomatic: the people may prosper, but that will not relieve the state's poverty.

sentences.zh: 唯簡費去華，專在節儉，求贍之道，莫此為貴耳。」

translations.literal: Only to reduce expenses and remove extravagance, focusing on thrift — of ways to seek sufficiency, none is more valued than this."
translations.idiomatic: The answer is to cut spending, abandon extravagance, and practice frugality — no remedy is more essential."

sentences.zh: 議者又以為「銅轉難得，欲鑄二銖錢。」

translations.literal: Those in the deliberation further argued that "copper is growing harder to obtain; they wished to cast two-zhu coins."
translations.idiomatic: Others argued that copper was growing scarce and proposed minting two-zhu coins."

sentences.zh: 竣曰：「議者以為官藏空虛，宜更改鑄；

translations.literal: Jun said: "Those in the deliberation hold that the treasury is empty and the coinage ought to be changed;
translations.idiomatic: Jun replied: "The advisers say the treasury is empty and the currency should be reformed;

sentences.zh: 天下銅少，宜減錢式以救交弊，賑國舒民。

translations.literal: copper under Heaven is scarce; the coin standard ought to be reduced to rescue trade disorders, relieve the state, and ease the people.
translations.idiomatic: copper is scarce nationwide, and reducing coin weight would ease trade, relieve the state, and help the people.

sentences.zh: 愚以為不然。

translations.literal: I consider this wrong.
translations.idiomatic: I disagree.

sentences.zh: 今鑄二銖，恣行新細，於官無解於乏，而民間奸巧大興，天下之貨將糜碎至盡；

translations.literal: Now to cast two-zhu and let new thin coins run freely — for the government it does not resolve want, while among the people cunning and fraud will rise greatly, and goods under Heaven will be ground to fragments until exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: Minting two-zhu coins and flooding the market with debased new currency would not relieve the treasury, but would unleash widespread fraud until the nation's currency was destroyed utterly.

sentences.zh: 空嚴立禁，而利深難絕，不一二年，其弊不可復救。

translations.literal: Empty strictures would be established while profit runs deep and hard to cut off — within a year or two, the harm could not be remedied.
translations.idiomatic: Prohibitions would be futile against such deep profit; within a year or two the damage would be irreversible.

sentences.zh: 民懲大錢之改，兼畏近日新禁，市井之間，必生紛擾。

translations.literal: The people, chastened by changes to large coins and also fearing the recent new prohibition, between market and lane will surely breed turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The people, still wary from past currency reforms and the recent ban, would surely throw the markets into chaos.

sentences.zh: 遠利未聞，切患猥及，富商得志，貧民困窘，此皆其不可者也。」

translations.literal: Distant benefit is unheard of; immediate harm arrives indiscriminately; wealthy merchants get their way, poor people fall into distress — these are all reasons it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: No lasting benefit is in sight, while immediate harm would fall on everyone — the rich would profit and the poor would suffer. These are all reasons to reject the proposal."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 魏定州刺史高陽許宗之求取不節，深澤民馬超謗毀宗之，宗之毆殺超，恐其家人告狀，上超詆訕朝政。

translations.literal: Wei Ding Province Governor Gaoyang Xu Zongzhi's demands were unrestrained; Shenze native Ma Chao slandered Zongzhi, and Zongzhi beat and killed Chao; fearing Chao's family would lodge a complaint, he reported that Chao had slandered the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zongzhi, governor of Ding Province in Wei and a man of Gaoyang, was unrestrained in his exactions; Ma Chao of Shenze denounced him, and Zongzhi beat him to death. Fearing the family would bring charges, Zongzhi reported that Chao had slandered the court.

sentences.zh: 魏高宗曰：「此必妄也。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong of Wei said: "This must be false.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong of Wei said: "This must be a fabrication.

sentences.zh: 朕為天下主，何惡於超而有此言！

translations.literal: I am sovereign of all under Heaven — what ill have I done Chao that such words should exist!
translations.idiomatic: I am sovereign of the realm — what wrong have I done Ma Chao to warrant such talk!

sentences.zh: 必宗之懼罪誣超。」

translations.literal: Surely Zongzhi, fearing guilt, framed Chao."
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhi must have feared punishment and framed Chao."

sentences.zh: 案驗，果然，斬宗之於都南。

translations.literal: Investigation verified it — so it was; Zongzhi was beheaded south of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation confirmed it; Zongzhi was beheaded south of the capital.

sentences.zh: 金紫光祿大夫顏延之卒。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon Yan Yanzhi died.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yanzhi, Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, died.

sentences.zh: 延之子竣貴重，凡所資供，延之一無所受，布衣茅屋，蕭然如故。

translations.literal: Yanzhi's son Jun held high rank and weight; whatever supplies were offered, Yanzhi accepted none of them — plain cloth and a thatched hut, desolate as before.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jun had risen to great power and wealth, yet Yanzhi accepted none of his gifts, living in plain clothes and a thatched hut as spare as ever.

sentences.zh: 常乘贏牛笨車，逢竣鹵簿，即屏住道側。

translations.literal: He regularly rode a lean ox in a clumsy cart; when he encountered Jun's guard of honor, he at once withdrew to the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: He usually rode a scrawny ox in a crude cart; whenever he met Jun's procession, he pulled aside to wait.

sentences.zh: 常語竣曰：「吾平生不喜見要人，今不幸見汝！」

translations.literal: He often told Jun: "All my life I have disliked meeting important people — now, alas, I must see you!"
translations.idiomatic: He often told Jun: "I have never liked meeting the powerful — and now, of all people, I must see you!"

sentences.zh: 竣起宅，延之謂曰：「善為之，無令後人笑汝拙也。」

translations.literal: When Jun built a mansion, Yanzhi told him: "Build it well — do not let later people laugh at your clumsiness."
translations.idiomatic: When Jun built a mansion, Yanzhi said: "Build it well — do not let posterity laugh at your lack of taste."

sentences.zh: 延之嘗早詣竣，見賓客盈門，竣尚未起，延之怒曰：「汝出糞土之中，升雲霞之上。

translations.literal: Yanzhi once called on Jun early in the morning, saw guests filling the gate, and Jun had not yet risen; Yanzhi angrily said: "You came up from the dung heap to the clouds above.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi once called early on Jun, found the gate packed with guests while Jun still lay abed, and said in anger: "You rose from the mire to the heavens.

sentences.zh: 遽驕傲如此，其能久乎！」

translations.literal: So suddenly proud like this — can it last long!"
translations.idiomatic: And already so arrogant — how long can that last!"

sentences.zh: 竣丁父憂，裁逾月，起為右將軍，丹陽尹如故。

translations.literal: When Jun completed mourning for his father, barely a month had passed when he was recalled as Right General, his post as Danyang Intendant unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's mourning for his father had barely passed a month when he was recalled as Right General and continued as Danyang Intendant.

sentences.zh: 竣固辭，表十上；

translations.literal: Jun firmly declined, memorializing ten times;
translations.idiomatic: Jun repeatedly refused, submitting ten memorials;

sentences.zh: 上不許，遣中書舍人戴明寶抱竣登車，載之郡捨，賜以布衣一襲，絮以彩綸，遣主衣就衣諸體。

translations.literal: the Emperor would not permit it and sent Palace Secretariat Attendant Dai Mingbao to carry Jun up into a carriage, convey him to the commandery quarters, gift him one suit of plain cloth padded with colored silk floss, and send a personal-clothing attendant to dress him from head to foot.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor refused; he sent Palace Secretariat Attendant Dai Mingbao to lift Jun into a carriage, deliver him to the yamen, gift him a plain robe padded with silk, and have an attendant dress him completely.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝武皇帝上大明元年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu the Founding Ancestor, upper fascicle — first year of Daming (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu, upper fascicle — the first year of Daming (

sentences.zh: 丁酉，公元四五七年）

translations.literal: dingyou, the year 457 CE)
translations.idiomatic: dingyou, 457 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛亥朔，改元，大赦。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the first day of the month (xinhai), the era name was changed and a general amnesty proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the first day xinhai, the era name was changed and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，魏主畋於崞山；

translations.literal: On renxu, the Wei emperor hunted at Guo Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, the Wei emperor hunted at Mount Guo;

sentences.zh: 戊辰，還平城。

translations.literal: on wuchen, he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: on wuchen, he returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 魏以漁陽王尉眷為太尉，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Wei made Prince of Yuyang Yu Juan Grand Commandant and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed Yu Juan, Prince of Yuyang, Grand Commandant and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 二月，魏人寇兗州，向無鹽，敗東平太守南陽劉胡。

translations.literal: Second month: Wei forces invaded Yan Province, advanced on Wuyan, and defeated Dongping Administrator Liu Hu of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Wei forces invaded Yan Province, advanced on Wuyan, and defeated Liu Hu of Nanyang, administrator of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 詔遣太子左衛率薛安都將騎兵，東陽太守沈法系將水軍，向彭城以御之，並受徐州刺史申坦節度。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard Xue Andu to lead cavalry and Dongyang Administrator Shen Faxi to lead naval forces toward Pengcheng to meet them, both under the direction of Xu Province Governor Shen Tan.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Xue Andu, Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, to lead cavalry and Shen Faxi, administrator of Dongyang, to lead naval forces toward Pengcheng, both under Xu Province Governor Shen Tan.

sentences.zh: 比至，魏兵已去。

translations.literal: By the time they arrived, the Wei army had already departed.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they arrived, the Wei forces had already withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 先是，群盜聚任城荊榛中，累世為患，謂之「任榛」。

translations.literal: Earlier, bandits had gathered in the thorn thickets of Rencheng, a plague for generations — called the "Ren Thickets."
translations.idiomatic: Bandits had long lurked in the thicket of Rencheng, a scourge for generations known as the "Ren Thickets."

sentences.zh: 申坦請回軍討之，上許之。

translations.literal: Shen Tan requested to turn the army back to suppress them; the Emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tan asked to turn back and suppress them; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 任榛聞之，皆逃散。

translations.literal: When the Ren Thickets heard of it, all fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the Ren Thickets bandits fled and dispersed.

sentences.zh: 時天旱，人馬渴乏，無功而還。

translations.literal: At the time drought prevailed; men and horses were parched and exhausted — they returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: A drought left men and horses exhausted; the expedition returned empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 安都、法系坐白衣領職。

translations.literal: Andu and Faxi were punished to serve in office wearing white.
translations.idiomatic: Andu and Faxi were demoted to serve in civil capacity without official insignia.

sentences.zh: 坦當誅，群臣為請，莫能得。

translations.literal: Tan was to be executed; the ministers pleaded on his behalf but could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Tan faced execution; ministers pleaded for him in vain.

sentences.zh: 沈慶之抱坦哭於市曰：「汝無罪而死。

translations.literal: Shen Qingzhi embraced Tan and wept in the marketplace, saying: "You die though guiltless.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi embraced Tan and wept in the marketplace: "You die innocent.

sentences.zh: 我哭汝於市，行當就汝矣！」

translations.literal: I weep for you in the marketplace — soon I shall join you!"
translations.idiomatic: I weep for you here — soon I shall follow you to the grave!"

sentences.zh: 有司以聞，上乃免之。

translations.literal: The responsible officials reported it; the Emperor thereupon pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was reported; the emperor then spared Tan.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚申，魏主畋於松山；

translations.literal: Third month, on gengshen, the Wei emperor hunted at Song Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengshen, the Wei emperor hunted at Mount Song;

sentences.zh: 己巳，還平城。

translations.literal: on jisi, he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: on jisi, he returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 魏主立其弟新成為陽平王。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor enfeoffed his younger brother Xincheng as Prince of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor enfeoffed his younger brother Xincheng as Prince of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 上自即吉之後，奢淫自恣，多所興造。

translations.literal: Since completing mourning and taking the throne, the Emperor had been extravagant and licentious at will, undertaking many constructions.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning and taking the throne, the emperor indulged in extravagance and launched many building projects.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹顏竣以籓朝舊臣，數懇切諫爭，無所迴避，上浸不悅。

translations.literal: Danyang Intendant Yan Jun, as an old minister of the princely court, repeatedly remonstrated earnestly and without evasion; the Emperor grew gradually displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun, Danyang Intendant and an old minister from the prince's household, remonstrated repeatedly and bluntly; the emperor grew increasingly displeased.

sentences.zh: 竣自謂才足干時，恩舊莫比，當居中永執朝政；

translations.literal: Jun considered his talent sufficient to manage the age, his favor and seniority unmatched — he ought to remain at the center and hold court affairs forever;
translations.idiomatic: Jun believed his talent and favor unmatched — he expected to remain at court and govern indefinitely;

sentences.zh: 而所陳多不納，疑上欲疏之，乃求外出以佔上意。

translations.literal: yet much of what he submitted was not accepted; suspecting the Emperor wished to distance him, he requested an outside post to gauge the Emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: but the emperor rejected much of his advice; suspecting he was being sidelined, Jun requested a provincial post to test the emperor's intentions.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，丁亥，詔以竣為東揚州刺史，竣始大懼。

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month, on dinghai, an edict appointed Jun Eastern Yang Province Governor; Jun then grew greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth month, on dinghai, an edict made Jun governor of Eastern Yang Province — and Jun was terrified.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，魏主如陰山。

translations.literal: On guimao, the Wei emperor went to Yin Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, the Wei emperor traveled to Mount Yin.

sentences.zh: 雍州所統多僑郡縣，刺史王玄謨上言：「僑郡縣無有境土，新舊錯亂，租課不時，請皆土斷。」

translations.literal: Under Yong Province's jurisdiction were many refugee counties and commanderies; Governor Wang Xuemo memorialized: "The refugee counties and commanderies have no territorial boundaries; old and new are confused, and land tax is not collected on time — I request territorial registration for all."
translations.idiomatic: Yong Province governed many refugee districts; Governor Wang Xuemo memorialized: "Refugee districts have no fixed territory, old and new registrations overlap, and taxes go uncollected — I request a comprehensive land registration."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛未，詔並雍州三郡十六縣為一郡。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on xinwei, an edict merged three commanderies and sixteen counties of Yong Province into one commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinwei, an edict merged three commanderies and sixteen counties in Yong Province into one.

sentences.zh: 郡縣流民不願屬籍，訛言玄謨欲反。

translations.literal: Refugees in the counties and commanderies did not wish to be registered; a false rumor spread that Xuemo intended rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Displaced people resisted registration, and rumors spread that Xuemo planned to rebel.

sentences.zh: 時柳元景宗強，群從多為雍部二千石，乘聲皆欲討玄謨。

translations.literal: At the time the Liu clan of Liu Yuanjing was powerful; many cousins served as two-thousand-bushel officials in Yong Province and, riding the rumor, all wished to attack Xuemo.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu clan of Liu Yuanjing was powerful; many kinsmen held posts in Yong Province and, seizing on the rumor, wished to move against Xuemo.

sentences.zh: 玄謨令內外晏然以解眾惑，馳使啟上，具陳本末。

translations.literal: Xuemo ordered inner and outer calm to dispel the crowd's confusion and sent a fast messenger to report to the Emperor, fully setting forth cause and effect.
translations.idiomatic: Xuemo kept both court and province calm to quell the panic and sent an urgent report to the emperor explaining everything.

sentences.zh: 上知其虛，遣主書吳喜撫慰之，且報曰：「七十老公，反欲何求！

translations.literal: The Emperor knew it was false, sent Chief Secretary Wu Xi to comfort him, and also replied: "A seventy-year-old man — what would rebellion seek!
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the rumors false, the emperor sent Chief Secretary Wu Xi to reassure him with a message: "You're seventy years old — what could rebellion possibly gain you!

sentences.zh: 君臣之際，足以相保，聊復為笑，伸卿眉頭耳。」

translations.literal: Between lord and minister, protection is assured enough; this is merely a jest again, to unwrinkle your brow."
translations.idiomatic: Between sovereign and minister, trust is enough; this is only a jest to make you smile."

sentences.zh: 玄謨性嚴，未嘗妄笑，故上以此戲之。

translations.literal: Xuemo's nature was stern; he never laughed lightly — therefore the Emperor teased him thus.
translations.idiomatic: Xuemo was stern and rarely smiled — hence the emperor's playful reply.

sentences.zh: 八月，己亥，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on jihai, the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jihai, the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，徙司空、南徐州刺史竟陵王誕為南兗州刺史，以太子詹事劉延孫為南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Minister of Works and Southern Xu Province Governor Prince of Jingling Dan was transferred to Southern Yan Province Governor; Crown Prince Household Steward Liu Yansun was made Southern Xu Province Governor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Prince Dan of Jingling, Minister of Works and governor of Southern Xu Province, was transferred to Southern Yan Province; Liu Yansun, Crown Prince Household Steward, became governor of Southern Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖遺詔，以京口要地，去建康密邇，自非宗室近親，不得居之。

translations.literal: Initially, Emperor Gaozu's testamentary edict held that Jingkou was a vital place, close to Jiankang — unless one were an imperial-clan close relative, one could not hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu's will had declared Jingkou a vital post close to Jiankang — only close imperial kin could hold it.

sentences.zh: 延孫之先雖與高祖同源，而高祖屬彭城，延孫屬莒縣，從來不序昭穆。

translations.literal: Though Yansun's ancestors shared origin with Emperor Gaozu, the Gaozu line belonged to Pengcheng and Yansun's to Juxian — they had never been ranked in seniority by lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yansun's clan shared Gaozu's origin, Gaozu's line was Pengcheng and Yansun's Juxian — they had never been ranked as kin.

sentences.zh: 上既命延孫鎮京口，仍詔與延孫合族，使諸王皆序長幼。

translations.literal: The Emperor, having ordered Yansun to garrison Jingkou, further issued an edict merger of clans with Yansun, making all princes rank by seniority and juniority.
translations.idiomatic: Having posted Yansun at Jingkou, the emperor ordered him incorporated into the imperial clan and had all princes ranked by seniority.

sentences.zh: 上閨門無禮，不擇親疏、尊卑，流聞民間，無所不至。

translations.literal: The Emperor's inner quarters were without propriety — he did not choose between near and distant, high and low; reports reached the common people, reaching everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's conduct in the inner palace was scandalous — heedless of kinship or rank — and rumors spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 誕寬而有禮，又誅太子劭、丞相義宣皆有大功，人心竊向之。

translations.literal: Dan was generous and possessed propriety; moreover he had great merit in slaying Crown Prince Shao and Chancellor Yixuan — in people's hearts they secretly turned toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was generous and upright; he had played major roles in suppressing Crown Prince Shao and Chancellor Yixuan, and public sentiment quietly favored him.

sentences.zh: 誕多聚才力之士，蓄精甲利兵，上由是畏而忌之，不欲誕居中，使出鎮京口；

translations.literal: Dan gathered many men of talent and strength and stored fine armor and sharp weapons; the Emperor therefore feared and resented him, did not wish Dan to remain at the center, and sent him out to garrison Jingkou;
translations.idiomatic: Dan gathered talented men and hoarded arms; the emperor feared and resented him, removed him from court, and posted him at Jingkou;

sentences.zh: 猶嫌其逼，更徙之廣陵。

translations.literal: still finding him too close, he further transferred him to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: still deeming him too near, the emperor transferred him again to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 以延孫腹心之臣，故使鎮京口以防之。

translations.literal: Because Yansun was a trusted inner minister, he was made to garrison Jingkou to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yansun, a trusted confidant, was posted at Jingkou to keep watch on him.

sentences.zh: 魏主將東巡，冬，十月，詔太宰常英起行宮於遼西黃山。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor was about to tour east; winter, tenth month, an edict ordered Grand Preceptor Chang Ying to erect a traveling palace at Huang Mountain in Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: As the Wei emperor prepared an eastern tour, in winter, the tenth month, an edict ordered Grand Preceptor Chang Ying to build a traveling palace at Mount Huang in Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁亥，更以順陽王休范為桂陽王。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on dinghai, Prince of Shunyang Xiufan was further changed to Prince of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dinghai, Prince Xiufan of Shunyang was re-designated Prince of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝武皇帝上大明二年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu the Founding Ancestor, upper fascicle — second year of Daming (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu, upper fascicle — the second year of Daming (

sentences.zh: 戊戌，公元四五八年）

translations.literal: wuxu, the year 458 CE)
translations.idiomatic: wuxu, 458 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙午朔，魏設酒禁，釀、酤、飲者皆斬之；

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the first day of the month (bingwu), Wei established a liquor prohibition — brewers, sellers, and drinkers were all beheaded;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the first day bingwu, Wei imposed a total ban on alcohol — brewing, selling, or drinking were capital offenses;

sentences.zh: 吉凶之會，聽開禁，有程日。

translations.literal: at assemblies for joy or mourning, the ban was lifted to permit drinking, with fixed days allotted.
translations.idiomatic: For weddings and funerals, limited exceptions were allowed on fixed days.

sentences.zh: 魏主以士民多因酒致斗及議國政，故禁之。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor, because gentry and commoners often caused brawls through wine and discussed state affairs, therefore prohibited it.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor imposed the ban because wine so often led officials and commoners alike to brawl and debate politics.

sentences.zh: 增置內外候官，伺察諸曹及州、鎮，或微服雜亂於府寺間，以求百官過失，有司窮治，訊掠取服；

translations.literal: He further added internal and external surveillance officers, to spy on the various bureaus and provinces and garrisons; sometimes going in plain clothes and mingling in government halls, seeking officials' faults; the authorities would exhaustively prosecute, interrogating with beating until confession was obtained;
translations.idiomatic: He expanded the corps of internal and external surveillance officers to watch every bureau, province, and garrison — sometimes infiltrating offices in disguise to catch misdeeds. Offenders were relentlessly prosecuted and tortured until they confessed.

sentences.zh: 百官贓滿二丈者皆斬。

translations.literal: Officials whose graft reached two zhang were all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Any official found guilty of bribery amounting to twenty feet of silk was executed.

sentences.zh: 又增律七十九章。

translations.literal: He also added seventy-nine articles to the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-nine new statutes were added to the legal code.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，魏如廣寧溫泉宮，遂巡平州；

translations.literal: On yimao, Wei proceeded to the Guangning Hot Spring Palace, then toured Ping Province;
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the Wei emperor went to the Guangning Hot Spring Palace and then toured Ping Province;

sentences.zh: 庚午，至黃山宮；

translations.literal: On gengwu, he arrived at Huang Mountain Palace;
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu he reached the Huang Mountain Palace;

sentences.zh: 二月，丙子，登碣石山，觀滄海；

translations.literal: Second month, on bingzi, he ascended Jieshi Mountain and viewed the Blue Sea;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingzi, he climbed Mount Jieshi and gazed upon the eastern sea;

sentences.zh: 戊寅，南如信都，畋於廣川。

translations.literal: On wuyin, he went south to Xindu and hunted at Guangchuan.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin he traveled south to Xindu and hunted at Guangchuan.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以金紫光祿大夫褚湛之為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Chu Zhanzhi, Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, was appointed Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Chu Zhanzhi, Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, was made Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，建平宣簡王宏以疾解尚書令；

translations.literal: On bingxu, Prince Xuanjian of Jianping, Hong, resigned as Director of the Imperial Secretariat due to illness;
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Prince Hong of Jianping, styled Xuanjian, stepped down as Director of the Imperial Secretariat because of illness;

sentences.zh: 三月，丁未，卒。

translations.literal: Third month, on dingwei, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingwei, he died.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，魏高宗還平城，起太華殿。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Emperor Gaozong of Wei returned to Pingcheng and began building Taohua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Emperor Gaozong of Wei returned to Pingcheng and began construction of the Taohua Hall.

sentences.zh: 是時，給事中郭善明，性傾巧，說帝大起宮室。

translations.literal: At this time, Attendant within the Gates Guo Shanming, crafty by nature, persuaded the emperor to undertake large-scale palace construction.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Guo Shanming, an Attendant within the Gates and a man of sly ingenuity, urged the emperor to launch grand palace building.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎高允諫曰：「太祖始建都邑，其所營立，必因農隙，況建國已久，永安前殿足以朝會，西堂、溫室足以宴息，紫樓足以臨望；

translations.literal: Palace Attendant of the Central Secretariat Gao Yun remonstrated: "When the Founding Emperor first established the capital, what he built was always done in the agricultural off-season; moreover the state has long been established — the Yong'an Front Hall suffices for court assemblies, the West Hall and Greenhouse suffice for banquets and rest, the Purple Tower suffices for viewing afar;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun, Palace Attendant of the Central Secretariat, remonstrated: "When the Founding Emperor first built the capital, construction always waited for the slack season in farming. The realm has stood for generations — the Yong'an Front Hall is enough for court, the West Hall and Greenhouse for feasting and repose, the Purple Tower for looking out over the city;

sentences.zh: 縱有修廣，亦宜馴致，不可倉猝。

translations.literal: Even if expansion is needed, it should be approached gradually — it must not be rushed.
translations.idiomatic: Even if enlargement is required, it should be carried out step by step, not in haste.

sentences.zh: 今計所當役凡二萬人，老弱供餉，又當倍之，期半年可畢。

translations.literal: By current estimate the labor required totals twenty thousand men; the old and weak to supply provisions would double that again; completion is expected in half a year.
translations.idiomatic: By present reckoning the project will require twenty thousand workers, with as many again among the old and weak to haul provisions — half a year to finish.

sentences.zh: 一夫不耕，或受之饑，況四萬人之勞費，可勝道乎！

translations.literal: If one man does not plow, someone may suffer hunger — how much less can the labor and expense of forty thousand men be fully told!
translations.idiomatic: When one man leaves the plow, others may go hungry — what then of the toil and cost borne by forty thousand men? Words cannot measure it!

sentences.zh: 此陛下所宜留心也。」

translations.literal: This is what Your Majesty ought to heed."
translations.idiomatic: This, Your Majesty, is what deserves your close attention."

sentences.zh: 帝納之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 允好切諫，朝廷事有不便，允輒求見，帝常屏左右以待之。

translations.literal: Yun was fond of blunt remonstrance; when court affairs were unsatisfactory, Yun would request an audience; the emperor would regularly dismiss attendants and wait for him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun loved to speak plainly. Whenever policy troubled him he asked for an audience, and the emperor would send attendants away and receive him alone.

sentences.zh: 或自朝至幕，或連日不出；

translations.literal: Sometimes from morning until evening, sometimes for days on end without emerging;
translations.idiomatic: Their talks sometimes ran from dawn to dusk, sometimes kept him closeted for days;

sentences.zh: 群臣莫知其所言。

translations.literal: the ministers did not know what was said.
translations.idiomatic: and the other ministers never learned what passed between them.

sentences.zh: 語或痛切，帝所不忍聞，命左右扶出，然終善遇之。

translations.literal: His words were sometimes painfully sharp; the emperor could not bear to hear them and ordered attendants to help him out — yet he always treated Yun well in the end.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun's words cut too deep the emperor could not bear them and had attendants escort him out — yet he always treated Yun with kindness afterward.

sentences.zh: 時有上事為激訐者，帝省之，謂群臣曰：「君、父一也。

translations.literal: At the time there were memorials submitted that were accusatory and provocative; the emperor reviewed them and said to the ministers: "Lord and father are one.
translations.idiomatic: Once, reviewing memorials full of denunciation and provocation, the emperor told his ministers: "Ruler and father are one and the same.

sentences.zh: 父有過，子何不作書於眾中諫之！

translations.literal: When a father has faults, why does the son not write a remonstrance in public!
translations.idiomatic: If a father errs, why does the son not rebuke him openly before the assembly!

sentences.zh: 而於私室屏處諫者，豈非不欲其父之惡彰於外邪！

translations.literal: Yet one who remonstrates in a private chamber in seclusion — is it not that he does not wish his father's faults to be known outside!
translations.idiomatic: But a son who waits for a private room to speak — does he not mean to keep his father's faults from the world!

sentences.zh: 至於事君，何獨不然！

translations.literal: As for serving one's lord, why should it be any different!
translations.idiomatic: In serving one's ruler, should it be any different!

sentences.zh: 君有得失，不能面陳，而上表顯諫，欲以彰君之短，明己之直，此豈忠臣所為乎！

translations.literal: When the lord has faults and merits, unable to state them face to face but instead submitting a memorial for open remonstrance, wishing to expose the lord's shortcomings and show one's own uprightness — is this what a loyal minister does!
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler errs, to fail to speak to his face yet submit a public memorial exposing his faults and displaying one's own integrity — is that the conduct of a loyal minister!

sentences.zh: 如高允者，乃真忠臣也。

translations.literal: One like Gao Yun — that is a true loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: A man like Gao Yun — that is a true loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 朕有過，未嘗不面言，至有朕所不堪聞者，允皆無所避。

translations.literal: When I have faults, he never fails to speak face to face; even what I cannot bear to hear — Yun never avoids it.
translations.idiomatic: When I err he never fails to tell me to my face; even what I cannot bear to hear he does not spare.

sentences.zh: 朕聞其過而天下不知，可不謂忠乎！」

translations.literal: I hear my faults yet the realm does not know — can this not be called loyalty!"
translations.idiomatic: I am corrected while the realm never learns of my faults — can that not be called loyalty!"

sentences.zh: 允所與同征者游雅等皆至大官，封侯，部下吏至刺史、二千石者亦數十百人，而允為郎二十七年不徙官。

translations.literal: Those who campaigned with Yun such as You Ya all reached high office and were enfeoffed as marquises; subordinate clerks who rose to provincial governor or two-thousand-dan rank also numbered several tens or hundreds — yet Yun remained a Court Gentleman for twenty-seven years without transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Men who had campaigned with Yun, such as You Ya, rose to high office and were enfeoffed as marquises; dozens or hundreds of their subordinates became governors or two-thousand-dan officials — yet Yun remained a Court Gentleman for twenty-seven years without promotion.

sentences.zh: 帝謂群臣曰：「汝等雖執弓刀在朕左右，徒立耳，未嘗有一言規正；

translations.literal: The emperor said to the ministers: "Though you hold bow and blade at my side, you merely stand — never a word of correction;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the ministers: "You stand at my side with bow and blade, yet you are only ornaments — not one word of honest counsel;

sentences.zh: 唯伺朕喜悅之際，祈官乞爵，今皆無功而至王公。

translations.literal: only waiting for moments of my pleasure to beg for offices and ranks — now all have reached noble and ducal rank without merit.
translations.idiomatic: you wait only for my good humor to beg rank and title, and now you have all reached princely rank without merit.

sentences.zh: 允執筆佐我國家數十年，為益不少，不過為郎，汝等不自愧乎！」

translations.literal: Yun wielded the brush to assist our state for decades, benefitting it greatly — yet never rose above Court Gentleman; are you not ashamed!"
translations.idiomatic: Yun served the state with his pen for decades to great benefit, yet never rose above Court Gentleman — are you not ashamed!"

sentences.zh: 乃拜允中書令。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yun was appointed Central Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Yun Director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時魏百官無祿，允常使諸子樵采以自給。

translations.literal: At the time Wei officials received no salaries; Yun regularly had his sons gather firewood to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Northern Wei officials drew no salary; Yun regularly sent his sons to gather firewood to make ends meet.

sentences.zh: 司徒陸麗言於帝曰：「高允雖蒙寵待，而家貧，妻子不立。」

translations.literal: Minister of Education Lu Li said to the emperor: "Though Gao Yun enjoys imperial favor, his household is poor — wife and children cannot support themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education Lu Li told the emperor: "Though Gao Yun enjoys your favor, his family is destitute — his wife and children cannot get by."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「公何不先言？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Why did you not speak of this earlier?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Why did you not tell me sooner?

sentences.zh: 今見朕用之，乃言其貧乎！」

translations.literal: Now that you see I am employing him, you speak of his poverty!"
translations.idiomatic: Only now that you see I am promoting him do you mention his poverty!"

sentences.zh: 即日，至允第，惟草屋數間，布被，縕袍，廚中鹽菜而已。

translations.literal: That same day, he went to Yun's residence — only a few thatched rooms, cotton bedding, a padded robe, and in the kitchen nothing but salted vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: That very day he visited Yun's home and found only a few thatched rooms, cotton bedding, a coarse padded robe, and salted vegetables in the kitchen.

sentences.zh: 帝歎息，賜帛五百匹，粟千斛，拜長子悅為長樂太守，允固辭，不許。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed, granted five hundred bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain, appointed eldest son Yue as Administrator of Changle — Yun firmly declined but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed, granted five hundred bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain, and appointed Yun's eldest son Yue Administrator of Changle; Yun pleaded against it but was overruled.

sentences.zh: 帝重允，常呼為令公而不名。

translations.literal: The emperor esteemed Yun, regularly calling him "Director Lord" without using his name.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held Yun in high regard and habitually addressed him as "Director Lord" rather than by name.

sentences.zh: 游雅常曰：「前史稱卓子康、劉文饒之為人，褊心者或不之信。

translations.literal: You Ya often said: "Former histories praise the character of Zhuo Zikang and Liu Wenrao — narrow-minded men may not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: You Ya often said: "Earlier histories praise Zhuo Zikang and Liu Wenrao — the petty-minded may refuse to believe it.

sentences.zh: 余與高子游處四十年，未嘗見其喜慍之色，乃知古人為不誣耳。

translations.literal: I have been in company with Master Gao for forty years and never seen him show pleasure or anger — thus I know the ancients did not deceive.
translations.idiomatic: I have kept company with Master Gao for forty years and never once saw anger or delight on his face — the ancients did not lie.

sentences.zh: 高子內文明而外柔順，其言吶吶不能出口。

translations.literal: Master Gao is bright within and yielding without; his speech is halting and cannot get out.
translations.idiomatic: Master Gao is luminous within and gentle without; his words come slowly and with difficulty.

sentences.zh: 昔崔司徒嘗謂余云：『高生豐才博學，一代佳士，所乏者，矯矯風節耳。』

translations.literal: Formerly Minister Cui once told me: 'Master Gao has abundant talent and broad learning — a fine scholar of the age; what he lacks is bold, upright bearing.'
translations.idiomatic: Minister Cui once told me: 'Master Gao is richly gifted and deeply learned — a scholar without peer in our time; only bold, upright bearing is wanting in him.'

sentences.zh: 余亦以為然。

translations.literal: I too thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: I thought the same.

sentences.zh: 及司徒得罪，起於纖微，詔指臨責，司徒聲嘶股慄，殆不能言；

translations.literal: When the Minister fell into guilt, beginning from trifles — an edict pointed and rebuked him — the Minister's voice grew hoarse, his thighs trembled; he could scarcely speak;
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Cui was accused, the charge arising from a trifle, an imperial rebuke was read aloud — his voice broke, his legs shook, and he could barely speak;

sentences.zh: 宗欽已下，伏地流汗，皆無人色。

translations.literal: Zong Qin and those below prostrated themselves sweating, all without human color.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Qin and the others prostrated themselves, streaming sweat, faces drained of color.

sentences.zh: 高子獨敷陳事理，申釋是非，辭義清辯，音韻高亮。

translations.literal: Master Gao alone laid out the principles, explaining right and wrong — his diction clear and argued, his tone bright and resonant.
translations.idiomatic: Master Gao alone set out the facts, clarifying right and wrong in language lucid and forceful, his voice ringing clear.

sentences.zh: 人主為之動容，聽者無不神聳，此非所謂矯矯者乎！

translations.literal: The sovereign was moved by it; listeners all trembled in awe — is this not what is called bold bearing!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved; every listener sat awestruck — was this not the very bold bearing Cui had said he lacked!

sentences.zh: 宗愛方用事，威振四海。

translations.literal: Zong Ai was then in power, his authority shaking the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ai then held power, his might felt across the realm.

sentences.zh: 嘗召百官於都坐，王公已下皆趨庭望拜，高子獨升階長揖。

translations.literal: Once he summoned all officials to the capital hall — princes and dukes downward all rushed to the courtyard to look up and bow — Master Gao alone ascended the steps with a long bow.
translations.idiomatic: Once he summoned the officials to the capital hall; princes and dukes down rushed into the courtyard to bow — Master Gao alone climbed the steps and gave a formal bow.

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，汲長孺可以臥見衛青，何抗禮之有！

translations.literal: Viewed thus, Ji Changru could receive Wei Qing lying down — what violation of protocol is there!
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, when Ji Changru received Wei Qing reclining, where was the breach of propriety!

sentences.zh: 此非所謂風節者乎！

translations.literal: Is this not what is called moral bearing!
translations.idiomatic: Was this not the moral bearing Cui had missed!

sentences.zh: 夫人固未易知；

translations.literal: A man is indeed not easy to know;
translations.idiomatic: A man's true character is hard to know;

sentences.zh: 吾既失之於心，崔又漏之於外，此乃管仲所以致慟於鮑叔也。」

translations.literal: I erred in my heart, and Cui leaked it outward — this is why Guan Zhong grieved deeply for Bao Shu."
translations.idiomatic: I misjudged him in my heart, and Cui misjudged him in public — this is why Guan Zhong wept for Bao Shu."

sentences.zh: 乙丑，魏東平成王陸俟卒。

translations.literal: On yichou, Lu Si, Prince Cheng of Dongping of Wei, died.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Lu Si, Prince Cheng of Dongping in Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲申，立皇子子綏為安陸王。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on jiashen, the imperial son Zisui was established as Prince of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiashen the emperor enfeoffed his son Zisui as Prince of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 帝不欲權在臣下，六月，戊寅，分吏部尚書置二人，以都官尚書謝莊、度支尚書吳郡顧覬之為之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not wish power to rest with subordinates; sixth month, on wuyin, the Director of the Ministry of Personnel was split into two posts, appointing Director of the Capital Bureau Xie Zhuang and Director of Revenue Gu Yan of Wu commandery to the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to let power concentrate in his ministers, in the sixth month, on wuyin, he divided the Ministry of Personnel directorship in two, appointing Xie Zhuang, Director of the Capital Bureau, and Gu Yan of Wu, Director of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 又省五兵尚書。

translations.literal: Also abolished the Director of Five Armies.
translations.idiomatic: He also abolished the post of Director of Five Armies.

sentences.zh: 初，晉世，散騎常侍選望甚重，與侍中不異；

translations.literal: Initially, in Jin times, selection as Regular Attendant of the Rapid Cavalry carried great prestige, no different from Attendant-in-Ordinary;
translations.idiomatic: In Jin times the Regular Attendant of the Rapid Cavalry had been a post of great prestige, scarcely inferior to Attendant-in-Ordinary;

sentences.zh: 其後職任閒散，用人漸輕。

translations.literal: afterward the duty became idle and scattered, and those appointed were gradually held in lower regard.
translations.idiomatic: but later its duties grew empty and appointments came to be held cheap.

sentences.zh: 上欲重其選，乃用當時名士臨海太守孔覬、司徒長史王彧為之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to restore weight to the selection, and therefore appointed the day's eminent men — Administrator of Linhai Kong Gui and Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education Wang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sought to restore the post's prestige and therefore named two celebrated men of the day — Kong Gui, Administrator of Linhai, and Wang Yu, Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 侍中蔡興宗謂人曰：「選曹要重，常侍閒淡，改之以名而不以實，雖主意欲為輕重，人心豈可變邪！」

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Cai Xingzong said to others: "The Personnel Bureau is important and weighty; the Regular Attendant is idle and light — changing the former in name but not in substance; though the sovereign's intent is to alter weight and lightness, can people's minds really be changed!"
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Cai Xingzong remarked to others: "The Personnel Bureau is vital; the Regular Attendant is ornamental. To swap titles without changing substance — even if the throne means to shift prestige, can men's minds be fooled!"

sentences.zh: 既而常侍之選復卑，選部之貴不異。

translations.literal: Soon the Regular Attendant selection was again base; the Personnel Bureau's prestige was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Regular Attendant was again a lesser post, and the Personnel Bureau's standing was what it had always been.

sentences.zh: 覬，琳之之孫；

translations.literal: Gui was grandson of Linzhi;
translations.idiomatic: Kong Gui was a grandson of Kong Linzhi;

sentences.zh: 彧，謐之兄孫；

translations.literal: Yu was grandson of Mi's elder brother;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu was a grandson of Wang Mi's elder brother;

sentences.zh: 興宗，廓之子也。

translations.literal: Xingzong was son of Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xingzong was a son of Cai Kuo.

sentences.zh: 裴子野論曰：「官人之難，先王言之，尚矣。

translations.literal: Pei Ziye remarked: "The difficulty of appointing officials — the former kings spoke of it, and it is indeed ancient.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ziye wrote: "The difficulty of choosing officials is an old theme — the ancient kings spoke of it long ago.

sentences.zh: 周禮，始於學校，論之州裡，告諸六事，而後貢於王庭。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, it began in the schools, was discussed in the districts, reported on the six affairs, and only then presented at the royal court.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Rites of Zhou, men were trained in schools, assessed in the districts, tested on the six virtues, and only then presented at court.

sentences.zh: 其在漢家，州郡積其功能，五府舉為掾屬，三公參其得失，尚書奏之天子；

translations.literal: In the Han house, provinces and commanderies accumulated records of merit and ability; the Five Offices recommended them as clerks; the Three Dukes weighed gains and losses; the Imperial Secretariat presented them to the Son of Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, provinces and commanderies tracked merit, the Five Offices recommended candidates as clerks, the Three Dukes reviewed their fitness, and the Imperial Secretariat reported to the throne;

sentences.zh: 一人之身，所閱者眾，故能官得其才，鮮有敗事。

translations.literal: on one person's account, what was reviewed was many — thus posts could gain the right talent, and failures were rare.
translations.idiomatic: many eyes examined each candidate, so offices gained able men and misappointments were rare.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉易是，所失弘多。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin changed this, and the losses were vast.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin overturned that system, and the damage was immense.

sentences.zh: 夫厚貌深衷，險如谿壑，擇言觀行，猶懼弗周，況今萬品千群，俄折乎一面，庶僚百位，專斷於一司，於是囂風遂行，不可抑止。

translations.literal: People of thick appearance and deep feelings, treacherous as ravines — choosing words and observing conduct, one still fears incompleteness; how much less when today myriad types and thousands of groups are suddenly judged on one side, and hundreds of officials are monopolized by one bureau — thus the clamorous wind proceeds, uncontrollable.
translations.idiomatic: Faces can mask hearts deep as gullies; even choosing words and watching deeds one still fears error — how much worse when myriad ranks and countless men are judged at a glance and a hundred offices depend on one bureau! Then clamor for office runs wild and cannot be stopped.

sentences.zh: 干進務得，兼加諂瀆；

translations.literal: Striving for advancement and gain, with flattery and slander besides;
translations.idiomatic: Men scramble for promotion and profit, piling flattery upon slander;

sentences.zh: 無復廉恥之風，謹厚之操；

translations.literal: no longer the wind of integrity and shame, nor the conduct of prudence and honesty;
translations.idiomatic: and the old winds of shame and sober duty disappear.

sentences.zh: 官邪國敗，不可紀納，假使龍作納言，舜居南面，而治致平章，不可必也，況後之官人者哉！

translations.literal: Official corruption and state ruin, beyond recording — even if Long served as Chief Counselor and Shun sat facing south, achieving good governance and peace could not be assured — how much less those who appoint officials afterward!
translations.idiomatic: Official corruption and national ruin follow beyond reckoning. Even if Long Yao were Chief Counselor and Shun sat on the throne, perfect order could not be guaranteed — how much less under later appointing officers!

sentences.zh: 孝武雖分曹為兩，不能反之於周、漢，朝三暮四，其庸愈乎！

translations.literal: Though Emperor Xiaowu split the bureau into two, he could not return to Zhou and Han — morning three, evening four — what use is it!
translations.idiomatic: Though Emperor Xiaowu split the bureau in two, he could not restore the Zhou or Han way — a change of names, not of substance — and what did it avail!

sentences.zh: 丙申，魏主畋於松山；

translations.literal: On bingshen, the Wei emperor hunted at Song Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the Wei emperor hunted at Song Mountain;

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚午，如河西。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on gengwu, he went to Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on gengwu he traveled to Hexi.

sentences.zh: 南彭城民高闍、沙門曇標以妖妄相扇，與殿中將軍苗允等謀作亂，立闍為帝。

translations.literal: Gao Du, a man of Nan Pengcheng, and the monk Tan Biao, whipping each other with delusive doctrines, joined Palace Guard General Miao Yun and others in plotting rebellion to install Du as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Du of Nan Pengcheng and the monk Tan Biao, inflaming one another with heterodox teachings, conspired with Palace Guard General Miao Yun and others to rebel and make Du emperor.

sentences.zh: 事覺，甲辰，皆伏誅，死者數十人。

translations.literal: The plot was discovered; on jiachen all were executed, the dead numbering several tens.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was exposed; on jiachen all were executed, several dozen dying in all.

sentences.zh: 於是下詔沙汰諸沙門，設諸條禁，嚴其誅坐；

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued to purge Buddhist monks, establishing various regulations and strict penalties;
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered a purge of the clergy, with new rules and severe punishments;

sentences.zh: 自非戒行精苦，並使還俗。

translations.literal: except those of rigorous ascetic discipline, all were made to return to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: all except the most austere practitioners were forced to return to lay life.

sentences.zh: 而諸尼多出入宮掖，此制竟不能行。

translations.literal: Yet many nuns frequented the inner palace — this regulation ultimately could not be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: But many nuns came and went within the palace precincts, and the measure could not be enforced.

sentences.zh: 中書令王僧達，幼聰警能文，而跌蕩不拘。

translations.literal: Central Secretariat Director Wang Sengda — bright and alert from youth, skilled in letters, yet unrestrained and unbridled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengda, Director of the Central Secretariat, had been clever and literary from boyhood, but wild and heedless of restraint.

sentences.zh: 帝初踐祚，擢為僕射，居顏、劉之右。

translations.literal: When the emperor first ascended the throne, he was promoted to Vice Director, ranking above Yan and Liu.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first took the throne he was raised to Vice Director, ranking above Yan and Liu.

sentences.zh: 自負才地，謂當時莫及，一二年間，即望宰相。

translations.literal: Confident in his talent and pedigree, he believed none of the day could match him — within a year or two he expected the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his gifts and lineage, he thought none could rival him and expected the chancellorship within a year or two.

sentences.zh: 既而遷護軍，怏怏不得志，累啟求出。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Protector of the Army, sullen and frustrated, he repeatedly petitioned to leave court.
translations.idiomatic: When he was moved instead to Protector of the Army he grew sullen and repeatedly asked to leave the capital.

sentences.zh: 上不悅，由是稍稍下遷，五歲七徙，再被彈削。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased; thereafter he was gradually demoted — in five years seven transfers, twice struck from rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took offense; over five years Sengda was transferred seven times and twice stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 僧達既恥且怨，所上表奏，辭旨抑揚，又好非議時政，上已積憤怒。

translations.literal: Sengda, shamed and resentful, submitted memorials with pointed rhetoric and loved to criticize current affairs — the emperor's anger accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated and bitter, Sengda sent memorials barbed with irony and loved to attack current policy, and the emperor's wrath mounted.

sentences.zh: 路太后兄子嘗詣僧達，趨升其榻，僧達令舁棄之。

translations.literal: A nephew of Empress Dowager Lu once visited Sengda, rushing to climb onto his couch — Sengda ordered him thrown off.
translations.idiomatic: A nephew of Empress Dowager Lu once visited Sengda and tried to jump onto his couch; Sengda had him thrown off.

sentences.zh: 太后大怒。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was furious.

sentences.zh: 固邀上令必殺僧達。

translations.literal: She persistently pressed the emperor to have Sengda killed without fail.
translations.idiomatic: She pressed the emperor relentlessly to have Sengda put to death.

sentences.zh: 會高闍反，上因誣僧達與闍通謀，八月，丙戌，收付廷尉，賜死。

translations.literal: When Gao Du's rebellion occurred, the emperor falsely charged Sengda with colluding with Du; eighth month, on bingxu, he was arrested and handed to the Court of Judicial Review, granted death.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Du's plot broke, the emperor seized the occasion to accuse Sengda of collusion; in the eighth month, on bingxu, he was arrested, tried, and granted death.

sentences.zh: 沈約論曰：「夫君子、小人，類物之能稱，蹈道則為君子，違之則為小人。

translations.literal: Shen Yue remarked: "The gentleman and the petty man — classes that things can fit; tread the Way and one is a gentleman, depart from it and one is a petty man.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue wrote: "Gentleman and petty man are names that fit their kinds: walk the Way and one is a gentleman; leave it and one is a petty man.

sentences.zh: 是以太公起屠釣為周師，傅說去板築為殷相，明揚幽仄，唯才是與。

translations.literal: Thus Taigong rose from butchering and fishing to become Zhou's teacher; Fuyue left wall-building to become Yin's chancellor — they made the obscure and lowly bright and clear, bestowing office solely on talent.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Grand Duke rose from butcher and angler to become Zhou's teacher, and Fuyue left his mortar work to become Shang's chancellor — elevating the obscure and overlooked, appointing men for merit alone.

sentences.zh: 逮於二漢，茲道未革：胡廣累世農夫，致位公相；

translations.literal: Down to the two Han dynasties, this way was not changed: Hu Guang, farmer for generations, reached the rank of grandee and chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Down through the two Han dynasties this principle held: Hu Guang, whose family had farmed for generations, rose to grand chancellor;

sentences.zh: 黃憲牛醫之子，名重京師：非若晚代分為二途也。

translations.literal: Huang Xian, son of a cattle doctor, was famed in the capital — not like later ages, when the path was split in two.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Xian, a cattle doctor's son, won renown in the capital — not as in later times, when gentlemen and commoners were kept on separate tracks.

sentences.zh: 魏武始立九品，蓋以論人才優劣，非謂世族高卑。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei first established the nine ranks — broadly to judge talent superior or inferior, not to mark clans high or low.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao first instituted the nine-rank system to assess merit, not to fix the status of great clans.

sentences.zh: 而都正俗士，隨時俯仰，憑藉世資，用相陵駕；

translations.literal: Yet the directors and vulgar scholars, bending with the times, relied on inherited standing and used it to overtop one another;
translations.idiomatic: But the rank directors and conventional men, swaying with fashion, leaned on family pedigree to lord it over others;

sentences.zh: 因此相沿，遂為成法。

translations.literal: Thus passed down, it became established law.
translations.idiomatic: Passed down in this way, it hardened into fixed practice.

sentences.zh: 周、漢之道，以智役愚，魏、晉以來，以貴役賤，士庶之科，較然有辨矣。

translations.literal: The way of Zhou and Han employed the wise to command the foolish; from Wei and Jin onward, the noble commanded the base — the categories of gentry and commoners were clearly distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou and Han, the wise led the simple; from Wei and Jin on, birth trumped ability — gentry and commoners were sharply divided.

sentences.zh: 裴子野論曰：「古者，德義可尊，無擇負販；

translations.literal: Pei Ziye remarked: "In antiquity, virtue and righteousness were what commanded respect — there was no picking among peddlers and bearers;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ziye wrote: "In antiquity, worth won respect regardless of trade — peddlers and burden-bearers were not passed over;

sentences.zh: 苟非其人，何取世族！

translations.literal: if not the right man, what use were great clans!
translations.idiomatic: if a man lacked merit, of what use was a grand lineage!

sentences.zh: 名公子孫，還齊布衣之伍；

translations.literal: Scions of famous houses still stood level with common cloth;
translations.idiomatic: Sons of illustrious houses still ranked with commoners in plain dress;

sentences.zh: 士庶雖分，本無華素之隔。

translations.literal: though gentry and commoners were distinguished, originally there was no wall between ornament and plainness.
translations.idiomatic: gentry and commoners were known apart, yet there was no hard line between the splendid and the plain.

sentences.zh: 有晉以來，其流稍改，草澤奇士，猶顯清途；

translations.literal: Since Jin, the current shifted slightly — extraordinary men from the wild grass still shone on the clear path;
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin dynasty the tide had turned; men of talent from humble ground could still rise to office;

sentences.zh: 降及季年，專限閥閱。

translations.literal: descending to the late years, admission was confined to pedigree.
translations.idiomatic: by the dynasty's end, office was closed to all but pedigree.

sentences.zh: 自是三公之子，傲九棘之家，黃散之孫，蔑令長之室；

translations.literal: From then, sons of the Three Dukes looked down on households of the nine thorns; grandsons of Yellow Gate and Scattered Cavalry despised the homes of magistrates and chiefs;
translations.idiomatic: Then sons of the Three Dukes scorned ministerial families; heirs of court attendants looked down on magistrates' households;

sentences.zh: 轉相驕矜，互爭銖兩，唯論門戶，不問賢能。

translations.literal: they turned to mutual arrogance, vying over ounces and grains, discussing only family gates, never asking talent or ability.
translations.idiomatic: pride bred pride; they quarreled over petty rank and cared only for lineage, not merit.

sentences.zh: 以謝靈運、王僧達之才華輕躁，使生自寒宗，猶將覆折；

translations.literal: Take Xie Lingyun and Wang Sengda — talented yet reckless; had they been born of humble clans, they would still have been destroyed;
translations.idiomatic: Men like Xie Lingyun and Wang Sengda, brilliant but headstrong, would have been ruined even in humble birth;

sentences.zh: 重以怙其庇廕，召禍宜哉。

translations.literal: add to this relying on their patrons' shade — inviting disaster was fitting!
translations.idiomatic: leaning on powerful patrons they brought disaster on themselves — little wonder.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙巳，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on yisi, the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yisi, the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，魏大赦。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the Northern Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲戌，魏主北巡，欲伐柔然，至陰山，會雨雪，魏主欲還，太尉尉眷曰：「今動大眾以威北敵，去都不遠而車駕遽還，虜必疑我有內難。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on jiaxu, the Wei emperor toured north, intending to attack Rouran; reaching Yin Mountain, he encountered rain and snow; the Wei emperor wished to return; Grand Commandant Yu Juan said: "Now we have moved a great host to overawe the northern foe — the capital is not far, yet if the imperial carriage returns in haste, the barbarians will surely suspect we have internal trouble.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiaxu the Wei emperor marched north to attack the Rouran. At Yin Mountain he met rain and snow and wanted to turn back. Grand Commandant Yu Juan said, "We have brought a great army to overawe the northern enemy. The capital is close, yet if the imperial train turns back at once, the tribes will suspect trouble at home.

sentences.zh: 將士雖寒，不可不進。」

translations.literal: Though the officers and soldiers are cold, we cannot fail to advance."
translations.idiomatic: The men may be freezing, but we must press on."

sentences.zh: 魏主從之，辛卯，軍於車侖山。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor followed this; on xinmao, the army encamped at Chelun Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor agreed. On xinmao the army encamped at Chelun Mountain.

sentences.zh: 積射將軍殷孝祖築兩城於清水之東。

translations.literal: General of Accumulated Archery Yin Xiaozu built two fortresses east of the Clear River.
translations.idiomatic: General of Archers Yin Xiaozu built two fortresses east of the Qing River.

sentences.zh: 魏鎮西將軍封敕文攻之，清口戍主、振威將軍傅乾愛，拒破之。

translations.literal: Wei's General Who Pacifies the West Feng Jiwen attacked them; garrison commander of Qingkou, General Who Inspires Awe Fu Qian'ai, repelled and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's General Who Pacifies the West Feng Jiwen attacked them, but Fu Qian'ai, garrison commander of Qingkou and General Who Inspires Awe, repulsed and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 孝祖，羨之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Xiaozu was great-grandson of Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Xiaozu was a great-grandson of Yin Xian.

sentences.zh: 上遣虎賁主龐孟虯將兵救清口，青、冀二州刺史顏師伯遣中兵參軍苟思達助之，敗魏兵於沙溝。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Tiger Guard Chief Pang Mengjiao with troops to relieve Qingkou; Yan Shibo, Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, sent Army Aide Gou Sida to assist; they defeated Wei troops at Shagou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Guard Chief Pang Mengjiao to relieve Qingkou. Yan Shibo, governor of Qing and Ji, sent Army Aide Gou Sida to help, and they routed the Wei army at Shagou.

sentences.zh: 師伯，竣之族兄也。

translations.literal: Shibo was a clansman elder brother of Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shibo was an elder clansman of Yan Jun.

sentences.zh: 上遣司空參軍卜天生將兵會傅乾愛及中兵參軍江方興共擊魏兵，屢破之，斬魏將窟瑰公等數人。

translations.literal: The emperor sent General of the Ministry of Works Aide Bu Tiansheng with troops to join Fu Qian'ai and Army Aide Jiang Fangxing in jointly attacking Wei troops; repeatedly they defeated them and beheaded several Wei generals including the Duke of Kugui and others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent Works Aide Bu Tiansheng to join Fu Qian'ai and Army Aide Jiang Fangxing against the Wei forces; they won repeatedly and beheaded several Wei generals, including Duke Kugui.

sentences.zh: 十一月，魏征西將軍皮豹子等將三萬騎助封敕文寇青州，顏師伯御之，輔國參軍焦度刺豹子墜馬，獲其鎧槊具裝，手殺數十人。
