translations.literal: Eleventh month: Wei's General Who Campaigns West Pi Baozi and others led thirty thousand horsemen to assist Feng Jiwen in raiding Qing province; Yan Shibo met them; Supporter of the State Aide Jiao Du stabbed Baozi and made him fall from his horse, captured his armored lance and full kit, and with his own hand killed several tens of men.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Wei's General Who Campaigns West Pi Baozi led thirty thousand cavalry to reinforce Feng Jiwen's raid on Qingzhou. Yan Shibo met them. State Aide Jiao Du speared Baozi from his horse, seized his armored lance and full panoply, and killed dozens of men with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 度，本南安氐也。

translations.literal: Du was originally of the Di of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Du was originally a Di tribesman of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 魏主自將騎十萬、車十五萬兩擊柔然，度大漠，旌旗千里。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor personally led one hundred thousand horsemen and one hundred fifty thousand carts against Rouran, crossed the great desert — banners and flags for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor personally led one hundred thousand cavalry and one hundred fifty thousand wagons against the Rouran, crossing the great desert with banners stretching a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 柔然處羅可汗遠遁，其別部烏朱駕頹等帥數千落降於魏。

translations.literal: Rouran Khan Chuluo fled far away; his separate division Wuzhu Jiatui and others led several thousand tents in surrender to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran khan Chuluo Khan fled far off; a detached branch under Wuzhu Jiatui and others led several thousand households in surrender to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏主刻石紀功而還。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor carved stone to record merit and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor erected a stone monument recording his victory and returned.

sentences.zh: 初，上在江州，山陰戴法興、戴明寶、蔡閒為典簽；

translations.literal: Initially, when the emperor was in Jiang Province, Dai Faxing of Shanyin, Dai Mingbao, and Cai Xian served as chief clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while the emperor was in Jiang Province, Dai Faxing of Shanyin, Dai Mingbao, and Cai Xian had served as chief clerks;

sentences.zh: 及即位，皆以為南台侍御史兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: upon accession, all were made Palace Attendants of the Southern Terrace concurrently Grand Clerks of the Secretariat for General Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession he made them all Attendants of the Southern Terrace and Secretariat General Clerks.

sentences.zh: 是歲，三典簽並以初舉兵預密謀，賜爵縣男；

translations.literal: That year, all three chief clerks, for taking part in the secret plan when arms were first raised, were enfeoffed as Barons of the County;
translations.idiomatic: That year all three were enfeoffed as county barons for their part in the secret plot that launched his uprising;

sentences.zh: 閒已卒，追賜之。

translations.literal: Xian had already died — the enfeoffment was granted posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xian had already died; the title was conferred posthumously.

sentences.zh: 時上親覽朝政，不任大臣；

translations.literal: At the time the emperor personally reviewed court affairs and did not entrust great ministers;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then handled state affairs himself and did not rely on his great ministers;

sentences.zh: 而腹心耳目，不得無所委寄。

translations.literal: yet for intimate counsel and eyes and ears, he could not fail to have someone to entrust.
translations.idiomatic: yet he still needed men he could trust for his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 法興頗知古今，素見親待。

translations.literal: Faxing was quite learned in ancient and modern matters and had long been personally favored.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing was well read in history and had long enjoyed the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 魯郡巢尚之，人士之末，涉獵文史，為上所知，亦以為中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: Chao Shangzhi of Lu commandery, at the lower edge of the gentry, having dipped into literature and history, was known to the emperor — he too was made Grand Clerk of the Secretariat for General Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Shangzhi of Lu commandery, a man of modest standing who had browsed literature and history, also won the emperor's notice and was made a Secretariat General Clerk.

sentences.zh: 凡選授遷徙誅賞大處分，上皆與法興、尚之參懷；

translations.literal: For all appointments, transfers, executions, rewards, and major decisions, the emperor consulted jointly with Faxing and Shangzhi;
translations.idiomatic: Appointments, transfers, executions, rewards — every major decision the emperor took up with Faxing and Shangzhi;

sentences.zh: 內外雜事，多委明寶。

translations.literal: internal and external miscellaneous affairs were mostly entrusted to Mingbao.
translations.idiomatic: day-to-day business, internal and external, went mostly to Mingbao.

sentences.zh: 三人權重當時，而法興、明寶大納貨賄，凡所薦達，言無不行，天下輻湊，門外成市，家產並累千金。

translations.literal: The three men's power weighed heavily in their time; yet Faxing and Mingbao took bribes on a great scale — whatever they recommended was invariably granted; the realm converged on them like wheel spokes; outside their gates a market formed; their household estates each piled up to a thousand jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: The three wielded enormous power. Faxing and Mingbao took lavish bribes; whatever they recommended was done. The empire streamed to their doors until a market stood outside; each man's household amassed fortunes of a thousand gold.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書顧覬之獨不降意於法興等。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Gu Yan alone did not lower his will toward Faxing and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Gu Yan alone refused to defer to Faxing and his circle.

sentences.zh: 蔡興宗與覬之善，嫌其風節太峻，覬之曰：「辛毘有言：『孫、劉不過使吾不為三公耳。』

translations.literal: Cai Xingzong was on good terms with Yan and disliked that his manner was too stern; Yan said: "Xin Pi once said: 'Sun and Liu could do no more than keep me from becoming one of the Three Dukes.'
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xingzong, who was friendly with Gu Yan, thought his standards too rigid. Gu Yan said, "Xin Pi once remarked, 'Sun and Liu could at most have kept me from reaching the Three Dukes.'

sentences.zh: 覬之常以為：「人稟命有定分，非智力所移，唯應恭己守道；

translations.literal: Yan always held: "A man's allotted fate has a fixed portion — it is not moved by intelligence or effort; one should only respect oneself and keep to the Way;
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yan always held that "each man's destiny is fixed and cannot be shifted by wit or effort; one should keep to the Way in humility;

sentences.zh: 而闍者不達，妄意僥倖，徒虧雅道，無關得喪。」

translations.literal: yet the ignorant do not understand, vainly hoping for luck — only wasting elegant principle, with no bearing on gain or loss."
translations.idiomatic: yet the dull do not see this and chase fortune vainly, debasing themselves for no real gain or loss."

sentences.zh: 乃以其意命弟子原著《定命論》以釋之。」」」」

translations.literal: He therefore charged his disciple Yuan to compose On Allotted Destiny to explain this.””””
translations.idiomatic: He therefore had his disciple Gu Yuan compose On Destiny to set out his views.””””
